1000010:
Beneath the surface, this turn-based roguelike RPG sends you into a labyrinth whose layout shifts as you take your turns. Each run builds a new maze, and you fight monsters in small locked rooms, so you never see the whole map and must choose how to approach each encounter. A crown grants powers, and elemental abilities are key to beating enemies.

Combat in Crown Trick is more a puzzle of positioning, skills and items than a test of reflexes. The game is single-player and follows the roguelike cycle of dying, learning and trying again, so it suits strategy fans who like thinking through every move.
1003890:
Set in 1950s New York, Blacksad: Under the Skin casts you as John Blacksad, a private detective drawn from a comic book series. A boxing club owner has died, and his daughter Sonia, now running the financially troubled gym, hires Blacksad to find Bobby Yale, a rising fighter who vanished before the biggest match of his career. The case leads through the city's grim underworld.

The characters are animal-like figures, which keeps the game close to its comic source while the mood stays that of a noir detective novel. It is a single-player adventure with full controller support, suited to players who prefer a mystery driven by investigation and conversation over fast action.
1004750:
The 2019 FIA World Rally Championship season is the basis for this official rally game, with 14 rallies and more than 100 special stages to drive. You race the clock across varied terrain, choosing tires and setups for each stage. A dynamic weather system brings rain and snow into play, changing traction as you drive and making the forecast worth checking.

The career mode in WRC 8 was rebuilt around running a team, with calendar planning, research and development, and a staff of mechanics, engineers and other specialists to hire. Online, weekly challenges and eSports events return. It suits rally fans who want a simulation-leaning challenge, and it has full controller support.
1016920:
Laying railway track faster than your train can run out of it is the whole challenge of this co-op game. Your team chops wood, mines iron and crafts rails in a randomly generated world while the locomotive keeps rolling forward, and a derailment ends the run. Each tool exists only once, so players have to split up jobs and coordinate constantly.

Worlds differ every time, and you can upgrade the train and attach wagons as the journey grows tougher. Unrailed! plays solo, online or on one screen, with PvP modes as well. The mood is frantic and funny, which makes it a good match for friends who enjoy cooperative games under pressure.
1029690:
Brittany, 1944: Karl Fairburne, an American marksman, joins a covert Rangers mission to weaken German coastal fortifications, teams up with the French Resistance and uncovers a secret project known as Operation Kraken. This third-person tactical shooter spreads its missions across large maps modeled on real locations, and you can approach objectives with long-range shots, stealth or direct fighting.

The series' trademark kill camera follows bullets in slow motion as they hit their targets. Beyond the single-player campaign, you can team up online or face other players in PvP modes. Sniper Elite 5 suits people who enjoy patient, methodical shooters with a World War II backdrop.
1045720:
Waking at night inside Sehwa High, student Mina Park finds her school warped into something sinister. Someone who resembles her teacher pursues her, so she must leave the building and cross the surrounding Sehwa district, solving puzzles, finding clues and meeting strange creatures and uncertain allies on the way.

This horror adventure from Korea is atmospheric and story-driven, and survival in The Coma 2 depends on evading a relentless threat while making use of whatever resources can be found. It is single-player and suits horror fans who enjoy narrative adventures set in a Korean school and neighborhood.
105000:
Climate catastrophe is closing in on Earth in this point-and-click adventure, presented in the style of a graphic novel. Bioengineer Bent Svensson, who left energy research to live quietly in the forests of Norway, gets an unexpected visitor: a woman named Fay, who says she has come back from the future. She insists his work on alternative energy is humanity's last hope, and the two must travel the world to see it through.

The tone balances a serious environmental premise with wit. This Final Cut edition from Daedalic Entertainment is single-player and suits adventure fans who prefer story and dialogue to action.
1057800:
Turn-based tactics and card-game deckbuilding are combined here. You follow Phoebe, a young inventor saving cash to leave her parents' house, and her robot-arm friend Carlton as they take odd jobs. Her latest invention projects knights from floppy disks onto the battlefield. Before each fight you choose which knights to bring and build a deck around them, then play cards each turn to carry out your plan.

Mixing and matching card combos is the heart of the game, and different knights support different playstyles. Floppy Knights has bright art and a friendly tone, is single-player and offers full controller support, so it suits anyone who enjoys deckbuilders or tactics games.
1060600:
Point-and-click puzzles and platforming are combined by giving you two characters to switch between. Ben is a devoted fan of old LucasArts adventures who collects odd items and combines them to solve puzzles, while Dan is an aspiring indie platform star who runs and jumps. Their different abilities work together as they try to stop several apocalypses that are all happening at once.

This one has a jokey, self-aware tone that pokes fun at both adventure and indie platformer conventions, and the pace is brisk. It is a single-player game, well suited to players who like clever item puzzles but also enjoy some platforming action.
1062830:
Rushing into burning buildings is the job in this chaotic firefighting game, where corporate crews put out flames, save people and salvage valuables. The 25 levels span three districts, and each is filled with hazards such as electrical faults, gas leaks and security systems you may need to evade. Earnings buy better tools, upgrades and outfits.

Embr can be played alone or with up to four players online, with difficulty adjusting to the size of the crew. LAN co-op and daily challenges are included. The tone is frantic and light, so it suits friends who like cooperative games where plans fall apart.
1067540:
Nordic folklore provides the setting for this adventure, in which you guide Tove through a snowy wilderness as she tries to save her family. You explore a forgotten world, collect curiosities and solve puzzles that open the way deeper into the cold. The monsters of local legend are not all enemies, and some can be befriended.

The story deals with loss and redemption, and the stylized, storybook look gives Röki the feel of a dark fairy tale. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who like atmospheric, exploration-driven adventures and are happy to move at a measured pace.
1069690:
The Devil is your character in this dark fantasy roguelike, back from hell and seeking vengeance against the Demon Hunters. Each run you lead a team of disciples, drawn from famous villains, through story events and turn-based battles, unlocking skills and building synergies between them. Collecting ancient artifacts is the route to your revenge.

Being the Devil means you can bend the rules of Rogue Lords itself at critical moments, which sets it apart from other turn-based roguelikes. Single-player with full controller support, it suits strategy fans who enjoy repeatable runs, team synergies and a villainous protagonist.
1071870:
Two small robots, Aku and Sila, travel across a planet side by side in this action-adventure built for pairs of players. Each robot's legs are steered separately, using a thumbstick or a mouse button per leg, and combining steps lets you walk, slide and operate machinery or even cut wood. Levels lead through icy mountains, waterfalls, valleys and forests.

Biped is designed around two players working in step, either on one screen or online, though it can also be played solo. The unusual controls make cooperation the point, and the mood stays friendly. It suits friends or family members after an easy-to-learn co-op adventure.
1072500:
This tennis simulation features real players from the ATP and WTA tours, such as Rafael Nadal and Ash Barty. Career mode has you climbing the world rankings in singles, or partnering a friend for doubles, while you look after your reputation and sponsors. A scenario editor lets you replay famous matches or build your own challenges.

Customization is a major draw in AO Tennis 2. An editing suite called the Academy builds your own player and courts, and you can also download creations from the community. Local and online multiplayer are supported, along with full controller support, making it a fit for tennis fans who like to compete with friends and tinker with content.
1076200:
Richard Garfield, designer of Magic: The Gathering, worked with the studio behind Faeria on this roguelike deckbuilder, in which you lead two heroes through the pages of a magical book that has gained a will of its own. You pick one of six hero pairs, then build a deck from cards, relics and abilities as you fight toward the legends waiting inside.

Two heroes fight side by side, and each brings a pool of more than 50 cards plus a personal relic, so different pairings favor different combos. Roguebook is single-player with controller support, and it suits deckbuilder fans who enjoy experimenting with synergies.
1082180:
Fast bikes and a dangerous road define this motorcycle racing simulation, built around the Snaefell Mountain Course, which runs for 60 km with tight bends and quick straights and ranks among the world's most dangerous races. You enter championships to prove yourself before attempting it, with 17 additional tracks, 18 motorbikes, classic models among them, and the official riders.

This sequel reworks its physics and rider movement for more realism and adds an open world where bike settings can be tested. Tuning and upgrades matter, and live data helps you stay competitive. It can be played alone or against others online, and suits motorsport fans who want demanding handling over arcade racing.
1085220:
Inside a human mind, Dusty, who embodies courage, and his ever-hopeful sidekick Piper head for Creed Valley, where ideals are formed, to repair a broken moral compass. Nightmares have overrun the once-peaceful lands, and you push back by solving puzzles, exploring varied environments and facing bosses in musical showdowns.

Each nightmare has its own theme song, so music is woven into the fights and the world. Figment 2 has a playful rather than grim tone, and a second player can join in local co-op. It fits families and anyone who likes imaginative, story-led adventures with a strong sense of sound.
108710:
Alan Wake follows a best-selling writer whose wife vanishes during a vacation in the town of Bright Falls. As he searches for her, he finds pages of a thriller he has no memory of writing, and a dark force begins to close in. Alan has to fight it off to find his wife while holding onto his sanity.

Combat, called Fight With Light, revolves around weakening enemies with a flashlight before finishing them off with firearms. The story is presented in episodes like a TV series, complete with cliffhangers and twists. This single-player thriller from Remedy suits players who value atmosphere and narrative.
1087760:
Rani is one half of a pair of struggling space haulers who land on an untouched planet teeming with life in this third-person action-adventure. The world holds the remains of a shattered civilization and a toxic parasite called the gunk, which Rani can clear away with a Power Glove as she uncovers secrets and works to heal the planet.

Exploration, puzzle solving and quick reactions all play a part in The Gunk, and the story follows the crew's changing relationship as mistrust grows between them. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to players who like narrative-focused adventures with an environmental theme.
1095120:
Death arrives early for Bjørn, a Viking who refuses to fight, in this narrative adventure with puzzle-platforming. After landing in Valhalla he is revived to help the mysterious Pesto retrieve a magical item. His undying body can detach and recombine its limbs at will, and you use that ability to solve puzzles and cross tricky levels.

Helheim Hassle shares a universe with Manual Samuel and takes a macabre approach, with friendship as a recurring theme alongside the body parts. Single-player with full controller support, it suits players who like quirky puzzle platformers with a dark sense of humor.
1107300:
Stranded for decades in the Bermuda after an unnatural storm, aviator Milton must find a way home in this quirky puzzle adventure. Caught in a bubble of time, he relies on you to escape each of six islands, where you crack codes, solve puzzles and collect magic orbs. Every island leads to the next as the search continues.

Along the way you deal with sea creatures and uncover secrets about the islands. Down in Bermuda comes from Yak & Co, the studio behind Agent A, and keeps a light, offbeat approach. Single-player with full controller support, it suits puzzle fans who want something relaxed and inventive.
1107750:
Raug Zeekon, an interstellar archaeologist, is sent by his company to investigate a mysterious signal from an unexplored star in this first-person puzzle game. On arrival he finds the Bia-Tool, an alien relic shaped like a pistol that can absorb energy and send it to other machinery. Using it, you work through temples and solve puzzles that get tougher the deeper you go.

Progress comes from routing energy between devices, which rewards observation and logic. Single-player with full controller support, Faraday Protocol suits players who enjoy methodical, thought-heavy puzzle games and discovering how an unfamiliar tool works.
1108590:
Boss fights are the heart of this fast, demanding soulslike, in which a lone warrior with an obsidian greatsword confronts the Old Gods. After humans rose up and imprisoned the gods in the Citadel, the gods struck back with a Desolation that leaves mankind fading. Defeating each one may grant powers beyond ordinary human limits.

Eldest Souls concentrates on boss encounters, with each colossal enemy presenting a different challenge. Combat is quick, so timing and learning attack patterns matter. Single-player with full controller support, it suits players who enjoy punishing boss fights in the soulslike mold.
1122340:
Both the business side and the cooking fall to you in this restaurant simulator. You assemble a kitchen from cooking surfaces, ovens and other equipment, hire staff, order ingredients from suppliers, set the menu and decorate, then step behind the stove for service. Finances and forecasts of how busy the evening will be help you avoid being swamped.

The menu draws on French, Italian and international dishes, which you can refine and adjust to the seasons and what customers expect. The long-term goal is recognition from the Michelin Guide. Chef Life is a single-player management sim that suits players who enjoy balancing planning and numbers with hands-on cooking.
1135910:
Open plains in Colorado, a Texas desert and forests in Eastern Europe make up the hunting grounds of this open-world simulation. You head out with a dog at your side, read tracks and trail any of 33 species. More than 160 licensed guns, gear and clothing items from brands such as Browning, Winchester and Bushnell let you set up your kit before each trip.

Realism is the focus, with animals that behave believably and a need to aim carefully so the trophy is not ruined. You choose from several dog breeds, including the Labrador Retriever. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to hunting-sim fans who value patient tracking over fast action.
1142710:
Closing out a trilogy that began with Total War: WARHAMMER, this strategy game pairs a campaign map with large real-time battles in the Warhammer fantasy setting. The story turns toward the Realm of Chaos, where a portal opened by a dying god's roar lets the Ruinous Powers loose to spread despair. Kislev and Grand Cathay stand in their way.

The roster offers seven distinct races and a large range of units, and you command armies in real-time clashes. Options include single-player, co-op and PvP multiplayer. It suits strategy fans who like large-scale battles and managing an empire, especially those who have followed the earlier games.
1153640:
Nara, a former warrior of a cult called the Circle, is now its most wanted fugitive and pilots Forsaken, a sentient starfighter, in this space-combat shooter. She is determined to destroy the cult and its leader, the Great Prophet, and her quest crosses the galaxy, passes through ancient temples and reaches places beyond waking reality. Along the way you unlock weapons and unusual abilities for zero-gravity dogfights.

The story is about redemption for a haunted past, and the bond between pilot and ship is central in Chorus. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who enjoy fast flight-based action with a narrative thread and a mystical edge.
1154810:
Failed tech startups literally sink underground in this satirical action dungeon crawler, and their cursed employees wander the halls as monsters. You play an unpaid intern working in Neo-Cascadia, a dystopian city, whose job is to descend into these ruins, defeat the monsters and repossess the company's assets, using office junk as weapons.

The procedurally generated dungeons are each themed on a type of failed startup, such as gig work, dating sites and cryptocurrency, and the humor in Going Under pokes fun at tech hype. Single-player with full controller support, it suits players who enjoy action-oriented dungeon runs with a comedic voice.
115800:
Floating islands in the sky are the setting for this story-driven platform adventure. You play Otus, a mute young owl who struggles to meet the expectations of his people, and whose troubles deepen when sky pirates appear. Otus can fly and carry objects and companions, and his friends act as gunners who fight alongside him, each with unique abilities.

The journey leads through monster-filled ruins with secrets and unexpected encounters. Owlboy's pixel art is a highlight, drawn with a great deal of detail, and flight is blended with platforming and combat. A single-player game with full controller support, it suits players who love retro-style visuals and emotional storytelling.
1158890:
Towers rise out of darkness in this cinematic puzzle-platformer, where a young Ravengirl, stuck on the lowest rung of a brutal, oppressive society, tries to escape. To get out, she must dodge machinery that would grind her up, cross rickety structures over deep voids and slip past guards ready to shoot her.

Her journey takes her from the city's highest points to its lowest depths, a path of discovery that leads to the remaining free people. The mood in White Shadows is bleak and the pacing cinematic. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to fans of atmospheric puzzle-platformers with dark themes.
1175460:
Reclaiming lost memories means climbing a clock tower in this fast twin-stick roguelite platformer, where an unnamed child moves through procedurally generated encounter rooms and boss fights. Dashing, wall sliding and twin-stick shooting form the base toolset, and power-ups and items found on each run upgrade the arsenal.

A distinctive feature is the health-for-power system: you trade health for strength, which makes you a glass cannon who must balance offense and defense. Options let you slow time, outline enemies in a color and set the amount of aim assist. Revita is single-player with controller support, and it suits fans of quick, repeatable runs.
1175840:
Escaping a magical prison drives this hand-painted point-and-click adventure, in which Vincent is joined by a friendly ghost named Nick. To find a way out you meet the eccentric locals, and each level offers at least two solutions: stealing from people or helping them. Branching dialogue affects your relationships with the locals and with Nick.

Whateverland is non-linear, with chapters playable in any order, plus mini games and a turn-based board game. The choices you make lead to different endings, which encourages replays. It is a single-player game, suited to adventure fans who enjoy dialogue choices and a bizarre fantasy setting.
1186640:
Evil has a pumpkin-headed champion in this spooky 3D platformer, which stars Jack, a mythical pumpkin lord working against the forces of good. The journey takes him through otherworldly landscapes, each with its own color palette and atmosphere. Combat relies on combos, dodging and good timing, and you unlock weapons and choose carefully which to use.

Physics-based puzzles built on gravity and reflection break up the action, and Jack can ditch his body and use his flaming head for jobs like burning books. The tone is playful and seasonal, with a Halloween mood. Single-player with full controller support, it suits platformer fans who like combat, puzzles and cartoon-style spookiness.
1190000:
Starting with a single new garage, you grow a service business in Car Mechanic Simulator 2021. Orders keep arriving, and you handle them by taking cars apart, testing, replacing parts, painting, tuning and rebuilding, working with more than 4,000 unique parts across over 72 cars. An auction house lets you buy vehicles in various conditions, and barn finds may hide valuable cars.

Income from jobs pays for new work spaces and better equipment, which widens the services you can offer. The emphasis is on detailed, hands-on repair, and it is played solo. It suits people who enjoy methodical tinkering and watching a small business grow.
1191900:
Saying NO to every absurd request is the whole idea behind this comedy, which bills itself as the first NPG, a No-Playing Game. You create a custom intern who starts a career in a quirky office, and your main action is shouting NO, which you can vary with different emotional tones and in several languages to knock colleagues off balance, then charge up for a stronger effect.

Controls are easy for newcomers to learn, and Say No! More follows a set path through the working day. The humor is silly and aimed at office culture. Single-player, it suits players who enjoy absurd comedy and want something easy to jump into.
1196090:
Dr Kate Ward is a scientist hauled across space to an unknown planet after a giant alien object shows up above Earth. Cut off from her crewmates, she crosses hostile ground on foot, shoots her way past strange creatures, and tries to piece together what happened to the team. It is a third-person shooter with a science-fiction mystery running underneath.

Combat is demanding and rewards patience over rushing in, so expect to learn from setbacks. The tone is tense and lonely, and the story unfolds at a measured pace. It suits solo players who want a tough action game with a plot to chase. It is single-player only and offers full controller support.
1196590:
Resident Evil Village is the eighth main entry in Capcom's survival horror series and a direct follow-up to Resident Evil 7. Seen through a first-person view, the story picks up a few years later with Ethan Winters and Mia, his wife, trying to build a quiet new life, until tragedy strikes again and Ethan is drawn into a remote village. Familiar figures return, including Chris Redfield, who appears in a menacing light.

Gameplay mixes first-person combat with tense chases and survival horror elements. It is a single-player experience with full controller support, suited to horror fans who want an action-leaning but still frightening entry, and to those who want to see Ethan's story continue.
1203710:
Classic stealth games get a humorous tribute in this 2D stealth action-adventure. You play Jesse Fox, held at a secret military facility for a crime he did not commit, who must escape using improvised gadgets, quick talking, explosives and, if needed, his fists. Taking down enemies quietly earns experience and skills, and you uncover a hidden plot as you work your way out.

At points, Jesse is interrogated by a lieutenant and recounts how the escape went, which feeds the comedy. UnMetal's tone is irreverent, with absurd moments such as impersonating a cat. Single-player with full controller support, it suits fans of old-school stealth action who like jokes with their infiltration.
1205170:
Jumping is off the table in this precision 2D platformer. Instead, the robot hero Magbot controls red positive and blue negative magnetic polarity, attracting himself toward platforms to cross gaps and repelling off surfaces to launch through the air. The goal is to rescue his homeworld, MagTek, from a villain tearing through the galaxy, and levels demand speed and accuracy.

Star fragments in hard-to-reach spots unlock extra challenges, and global leaderboards invite time-based competition. The 16-bit style visuals of Super Magbot recall classic console platformers. A single-player game with controller support, it suits players who enjoy mastering movement mechanics and replaying levels to improve.
1234430:
Memories of the First World War haunt a German soldier in this game of psychological horror. You alternate between two settings: a run-down, deserted manor that was your childhood home, where you wake in your teenage bedroom, and the trenches of the front line, where nightmarish creatures lurk among the horrors of war. As dream and reality blur, you work to reconstruct your past and break a cycle of suffering.

Fear and confusion drive the mood of Ad Infinitum, set against a war backdrop. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to horror fans interested in a historical setting and a story about trauma.
1252830:
Abby is a string puppet who performs in a circus and spends her nights locked in a cage. When she slips away, she enters a dark storybook land where freedom comes with risks. Her strings are part of the gameplay: you use them to solve puzzles, cross rivers, and evade bandits and traps.

The mood is dark but beautiful, in the manner of an old fairy tale, with a cinematic presentation and a story about hope and breaking free. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who prefer atmosphere and puzzle solving over fast reflexes.
1267540:
Kenya, Japan and New Zealand join the calendar in this official FIA World Rally Championship simulation, along with 35 new special stages and more than 15 classic cars. Drivers and cars from three WRC categories are included, and you tackle stages against the clock using updated physics, rebuilt engine audio and redesigned pacenotes that guide you through each corner.

A Clubs system lets players create their own championships and invite others to compete online, and custom championships are available to build as well. WRC 9 is aimed at rally enthusiasts who want a simulation-style driving challenge, and it supports single-player and online play, with full controller support.
1283400:
In an alternate 1789 Paris, King Louis XVI uses an army of automatons to crush the French Revolution. You play Aegis, a mechanical bodyguard built by the engineer Vaucanson for the queen, and fight through the city to change the course of history. Combat is demanding: you chain dodges, parries and jumps with strong attacks against mechanical soldiers, and the giant machine bosses call for patience.

Aegis can be developed toward different playstyles as you upgrade abilities. Steelrising is single-player with full controller support, and it suits fans of challenging action RPGs who like a historical twist.
1283410:
War has broken a kingdom of rats, and Redgi, next in line for the throne, must take it back from the Frog Clan and its leader Greenwart in this hand-drawn action RPG adventure. Along the way you rescue your brothers and meet companions who help with meal recipes, blueprints for forging weapons and armor, and even an armored mole vehicle. Combat is brutal and punishing.

The charming animal world hides a grim tone, and the narration by Doug Cockle, well known in RPG circles, adds weight. Single-player, Tails of Iron suits players who like challenging action RPGs with a storybook look.
1286680:
Guns, spells and swords share the stage in this fantasy looter-shooter from Gearbox, a spin-off of the Borderlands series, in which Tiny Tina guides you through a tabletop-style realm in which rules mean very little. You create a multiclass hero, then use guns, spells and melee weapons against outlandish monsters, collecting loot in dungeons and across a large overworld, on a mission to take down the tyrannical Dragon Lord.

Humor and chaos define the tone, with cross-platform multiplayer for partying up with friends, or the option to play alone. LAN co-op is supported. It suits fans of loot-driven shooters who enjoy a silly fantasy setting and like combining ranged and magic builds.
1287530:
Feudal economics drive this medieval city-builder. The crown tasks you with settling and governing new land by zoning plots, building houses, setting taxes and priorities, and growing supply chains as your population expands. Families are the core: each has a profession that determines what business it can run, and once you give them a plot and a house they work largely on their own, managing stock, setting aside produce for taxes and trading with others.

Because villagers buy and sell in a free market, supply and demand drive what goods are worth. You can also hold events and conduct diplomacy. Lords and Villeins is a single-player simulation that suits players who enjoy economic depth and watching systems interact.
1293170:
You steer a tiny robot, the ZX8000, through precisely built stages drawn in detailed pixel art. Running, jumping and dashing are the core moves, and new skills unlock as you go, with boss fights along the way and a cute story tying the levels together.

Karel Matejka, who goes by Ko.dll, made most of it alone, paying homage to classic platformers. Difficulty settings run from relaxed to punishing, so newcomers and veterans can both find a fit, and speedrunning lets you compete against other players for quicker times. It is single-player with full controller support.
1301950:
Travelling back to the 1990s as a small robot, you try to stop a tragic accident from happening inside your creator's home. The game is a side-scrolling, physics-based puzzle platformer, and you work through environmental puzzles while collecting upgrades such as boosters and harpoons.

Seen from a robot's scale, ordinary household items turn into landmarks and obstacles. The cute presentation and nostalgic music sit alongside a story about consequences: you may change the past, but you have to live with what follows. Single-player, with full controller support, and well suited to players who like thoughtful puzzle platformers with a story at their center.
1309620:
Maxwell Atoms, a spacetronaut marooned far from Earth, has had his DNA merged with that of a she-bear, and in this bullet-hell first-person shooter he can transform into a bear to fight. Your aim is to get home by blasting through robots hungry for oil across wastelands, space carnivals and ancient temples.

The tone is zany and retro-futuristic, with a large arsenal of outlandish weapons and gadgets, plus double jumps and dashes that keep the action moving. Fights favor constant motion over cover. It is single-player with full controller support, aimed at players who want loud, quick, tongue-in-cheek shooting.
1311510:
Jesper, a seventeen-year-old from the city, inherits a magical bracelet from his grandfather that gives him telekinetic powers. He travels to the dwindling fishing village of Slepp, on an island in Northern Norway, to learn where the bracelet came from and why his grandfather left. Light physics puzzles ask you to move objects, repair machinery and help the quirky locals.

The island is rendered in a calm low-poly style, and the puzzles are gentle, leaving room for the coming-of-age story centered on family, friendship and love. Your choices influence how that story unfolds. Single-player, with full controller support, and a good pick for players who prefer a warm, reflective adventure to a demanding one.
1335230:
Sumire, a girl who has lost her spark, crosses paths with a playful spirit in a Japanese village and strikes a deal: finish a list of tasks before nightfall and her biggest wish comes true. The requests come from woodland creatures, villagers and her own needs, and you choose which ones to accept.

Time is limited, and opportunities fade as the day moves on, so a request you refuse may never return. Collectibles, bonus items and skill-based challenges are scattered about, some of them hidden. The mood is magical and relaxed, and it suits players who enjoy narrative adventures with branching quests. Single-player, with full controller support.
1337010:
Alba spends a summer with her grandparents on an island in the Mediterranean, expecting quiet days of animal watching alongside Ines, her friend. Then she spots wildlife in trouble, and the holiday turns into a campaign to protect the place. You wander beaches, a town and an old castle, photograph animals, pick up litter and talk to locals while her birdwatching grandfather tags along.

It is a gentle, low-pressure adventure with warm, handcrafted visuals from ustwo games, the team that made Monument Valley. There is no combat or time pressure, just noticing wildlife and small acts of change. Families, younger players and anyone after a calm afternoon will feel at home. It plays solo with full controller support.
1338770:
Raven, a contract sniper assassin, is the role you take in this modern-warfare shooter, which sends you through a single-player campaign of hits across the Middle East. Each target calls for careful positioning, attention to distance and a precise shot, and some shots are taken from well beyond 1000 metres.

The game also includes Butcher's Banquet, an expansion adding a region called The Temple, with oases, waterfalls and temple ruins, plus a fresh set of contracts aimed at a dangerous leader known as The Butcher. It suits players who prefer methodical, long-range shooting to constant run-and-gun action. Play is solo only.
13600:
Ancient Persia is the setting for this third-person action-adventure. After a young Prince meddles with a magic dagger, the palace is overrun by creatures born from the Sands of Time. With a princess as his ally, he fights through the palace's chambers, combining acrobatic platforming, sword combat and puzzles, and uses the dagger's power over time to undo mistakes.

Originally released in 2003, the game is narrated by the Prince himself and follows a linear, single-player structure. Players who enjoy acrobatic traversal, timing-based challenges and a classic adventure feel will find a lot to like in it.
1364100:
You play Neil Conrad, an agent with the CDI, who is drawn into a murder investigation that could lead the solar system to war. You question people, collect evidence and decide how to act on what you learn, in an adventure driven mostly by conversation and set in a sci-fi noir future.

Choices branch the story toward different endings, and decisions are final once made. The 2D art leans into a noir atmosphere. It suits players who enjoy reading, weighing hard calls and replaying for other outcomes more than action. It is single-player with full controller support.
1367590:
Caroline Walker comes to the Winterlake mansion, now a hospital, when twin girls go missing, only to wake up in a bathtub wired to old medical equipment. From there, this survival horror game has her explore the derelict building, solve puzzles, manage resources and fight off the horrors between her and the truth.

The design follows the fixed-camera tradition of Alone in the Dark and the early Resident Evil games, with a dynamic camera and updated controls to smooth out the format. Expect slow, deliberate pacing and tense encounters. Single-player, with full controller support, and aimed at fans of classic survival horror who want that style with modern polish.
1383700:
Strapping a jetpack onto a caveman, this side-scrolling platformer sends him through a prehistoric world to stop an alien threat. Across 36 levels you fly over pits, smash through rock walls and club 30 types of enemies, with boss fights and fast flight sequences breaking up the platforming.

The caveman moves clumsily by design, so the challenge lies in mastering the jetpack and the abilities you gain over time. Arcade Mode raises the stakes with limited lives, checkpoints that no longer heal you and extra lives purchasable only between levels. The prehistoric sci-fi tone is colorful and light, suited to platformer fans who enjoy some difficulty.
1385100:
Every climb in Insurmountable is different, since this roguelike generates its mountains procedurally and ends your run for good if the climber dies. You pick one of three characters, each with their own skills and backstory, then keep vital stats out of the danger zone while searching crates, caves and old ruins for gear left by earlier adventurers.

Weather changes, day turns to night and random events add uncertainty, since you never know how an encounter will end. You descend as well as ascend, and every decision can matter. Single-player, aimed at players who enjoy tense survival and resource management and who accept losing a run now and then.
1395030:
Set in the 1990s, Kathy Rain is a point-and-click adventure built around a detective mystery. Kathy, a strong-willed journalism student, investigates the death of her grandfather and follows the clues he left in her rural hometown. You collect evidence, interrogate suspects, make deductions and solve puzzles, getting around on her motorcycle.

The Director's Cut revisits the 2016 original with a longer story, more puzzles and added locations. Beneath the mystery sits a personal story about Kathy confronting her difficult history. Single-player, with full controller support, and a fit for adventure fans who like dialogue-heavy detective stories with a grounded tone.
1410640:
Two women, living sixty-seven years apart, share one story. Kate Walker is a New York lawyer pulled into an unexpected journey, while Dana Roze is a talented pianist in Vaghen with a looming war hanging over her career. You switch between their eras, 2004 and 1937, travelling through cities in Eastern Europe.

Puzzles reward careful looking: you hunt for clues, mend broken instruments, open stubborn locks and coax old mechanisms back to life. Inon Zur composed the score, recorded with a Budapest orchestra. It is a slow, atmospheric single-player adventure for patient players who like mysteries and a strong sense of place.
1430680:
Pseudo is a martial artist who lives alone in Zenozoik, a bizarre land of odd creatures and strange cultures. When he meets a small being called the Boy, whose powers have caught Gemini's eye, he takes him under his wing and finds mercenaries on their trail. From there you travel the land and fight whatever stands in your way.

Combat is close-range and about timing: dodge, block, stun and counter, and switch to a first-person view for special techniques. The setting blends surrealism with punk-styled fantasy. It is a single-player action adventure from ACE Team, the studio that made Zeno Clash, suited to players who like melee fighting in a weird world.
1445790:
Course building is the hook in Make Way, a top-down party racer in the spirit of Micro Machines and Mashed. Between rounds, everyone picks pieces such as seesaws, loops, corkscrews and train crossings and snaps them onto the track. Then the cars race, dodging hazards, firing weapons and trying not to fall off the edge.

Courses keep growing until someone wins, and then a fresh one begins. You can cooperate on the layout or use it to sabotage rivals, and the chaotic tone suits groups of friends. Online player-versus-player matches and a solo mode are available, with full controller support. It fits players who prefer noisy, competitive racing to realistic simulation.
1446780:
Hunting giant monsters is the whole point of Monster Hunter Rise. As a hunter, you explore new maps, learn how each creature behaves and take it on with a choice of fourteen weapon types, then collect rewards from successful hunts to improve your gear.

The roster mixes returning monsters with new ones inspired by Japanese folklore, led by the wyvern Magnamalo, and a new storyline frames the hunts. You can play alone or team up in online co-op. The PC version adds visual and performance improvements. It suits players who enjoy learning enemy patterns and improving through repeated hunts.
1449320:
Writer Ed Miller survives a car crash in a California canyon and insists his family was with him in the vehicle, though the wreck holds no sign of them. He develops severe vertigo, and sessions with a therapist become his route toward what really happened. You play through the investigation from the viewpoints of three different characters, each with a story of their own.

The tone is unsettling and psychological, with themes of obsession, control and doubt about what is real. It echoes the look and narrative devices of classic suspense films and takes loose inspiration from Hitchcock's movie rather than retelling it. It suits single-player adventure fans who like slow-building dread.
1458300:
Neuroscientist Joshua Hayes belongs to a family hit by a rare condition that wears down the mind over time. Hoping to find a cure, he steps into parallel realities reached through deja vu, each built around a memory, some joyful and some painful.

The spaces he moves through are raw and minimalist, and items he comes across serve as doors into his past. An experimental program run by the biotech company Neuraxis draws him into corporate intrigue. Single-player, with full controller support, it is a story-first game with a serious tone, suited to players who want a reflective narrative about family and memory.
1462810:
Rally fans get the official game of the FIA World Rally Championship in an edition marking the sport's 50th anniversary. Alongside the 2021 season, which adds rallies in Spain, Estonia, Croatia and Belgium, a History Mode sets 19 historic events from across the decades, each with conditions that suit its era.

The package includes 120 special stages, fifty-two teams that competed in 2021 across WRC, WRC2, WRC3 and Junior WRC, and twenty classic cars from makers such as Lancia, Subaru and Toyota. A career mode and multiplayer, including online PvP and co-op, sit beside the solo racing. Developed by KT Racing, it suits rally enthusiasts who want a simulation with a historical angle.
1466230:
Cassiel is a foul-mouthed angel with six hours to stop Heaven from being destroyed, and she is stuck in a time loop while she tries. A magical clock from Death lets her jump to any point in the day, travelling between four realms, Heaven, Hell, Helheim and Earth, to uncover what lies behind a mysterious artifact made by God.

Time travel is the core mechanic: knowledge picked up later in the day can change what happens earlier, so planning matters. The tone is irreverent, from the creators of Manual Samuel, as well as Helheim Hassle. Single-player, with full controller support, and a match for players who enjoy time-loop puzzles and crude, comic storytelling.
1496590:
Rescuing her father from Meavora, the tyrant who rules an archipelago, drives Tchia's tropical open-world adventure, which draws on New Caledonia. The islands form a physics-driven sandbox that you cross by climbing, gliding, swimming and sailing, and a special gift called soul jumping lets Tchia inhabit birds, fish, dogs and many other creatures, as well as a large number of objects.

Meavora's fabric soldiers are met in open encounters where creativity counts for more than force, and a fully playable ukulele lets you jam along the way. The story is a coming-of-age tale with a poetic tone, and the pace suits wandering. Single-player, with full controller support, and aimed at players who enjoy sandbox play and free exploration.
1502560:
Gargamel's latest scheme is the Vileaf, a plant whose seeds trap Smurfs and whose toxins sicken the forest. Papa Smurf sends a team to gather ingredients for an antidote and free captured villagers, using the Smurfizer, an invention by Handy Smurf. You play as four Smurfs, Smurfette, Hefty, Brainy and Chef, across five worlds, healing sick plants while heading toward Gargamel's hovel.

This action-adventure offers split-screen co-op as well as solo play, so a friend or family member can join on the same screen. The cartoon setting, familiar cast and plant-healing mission make it a natural fit for families and younger fans of the Smurfs. Full controller support is included.
15320:
World War II flight simulation fills this collection, which combines the earlier games in the series, among them Forgotten Battles and Pacific Fighters, with the Ace Expansion Pack and campaigns set in an alternate 1946. What started as a study of a single aircraft has grown into a roster of more than 300 aircraft, 229 of them flyable.

A community-made update to version 4.12.2 adds widescreen support, extra aircraft, maps and scenarios, including new maps for Kiev, Manchuria and Burma. Multiplayer options include LAN co-op and PvP alongside the solo game. It suits dedicated flight sim fans who want an enormous range of aircraft and theaters of war.
1538850:
In Grotto, you take the role of the Soothsayer, the one person able to speak with the stars. When the valley's tribe hits hard times, its people seek your advice. From a sacred rock you look up, draw constellations and interpret what they say, and you can also read bones to predict the future or speak with the dead.

Your answers shape the tribe's fate, so each reading carries weight, and you can deliberate over every constellation or let intuition guide you. As you get to know individual villagers and their problems, the tribe may thrive or suffer depending on what you say. Single-player, with full controller support, and best for players who enjoy atmospheric, choice-driven storytelling.
1546710:
Vernal journeys through Haricot, a kingdom whose land rose into the sky as a chain of floating islands ruled by the Church of Aloe. She is searching for her estranged father and for the truth about her past, and Chervil, an automaton with no memory, travels with her. You explore towns and dungeons in 2D pixel art, defeating enemies and gaining new abilities that open up the map.

Quick combat and tight platforming sit at the center of play, while the story deals with a feud, a hunger for revenge and personal growth. It will appeal to Metroidvania fans who enjoy fast movement and a pixel-art look. It is single-player with full controller support.
1577120:
Summer camp at Hackett's Quarry is over for the year, and its nine teenage counselors celebrate with a party that quickly goes wrong. Locals covered in blood and something more sinister hunt the group. You play each of them in a cinematic horror story from Supermassive Games, making decisions that determine how events unfold.

Any counselor can survive or die before dawn, and relationships improve or fray under pressure, so each playthrough can take a different path. Banter and flirting turn into decisions where lives are at stake as the night worsens. It can be played alone or with others using shared-screen co-op, and suits horror fans who like cinematic, choice-driven stories.
1599020:
Marooned on Earth, Milo discovers he is far too small for the world around him, with every person gone and the calendar apparently stuck at 1991. To get home to his own planet and return to his proper size, he crosses a sprawling, human-scale world and recruits hundreds of tinykin, small creatures that each have a distinct power, to reach new places and solve problems.

Beyond the platforming and puzzle solving, the adventure is about uncovering what happened to Earth's people, and finding that out matters as much as the trip home. Single-player, with full controller support, it suits players who enjoy exploring colorful spaces and collecting things at a relaxed pace.
1608230:
Lana and her animal companion Mui live on a planet that was once in balance between people, nature and wildlife. That balance has broken: a faceless machine army has arrived, and the pair must lean on each other to survive and protect the people they love in this cinematic puzzle platformer.

The companion shapes how puzzles work, and the game mixes them with stealth and reflex-driven action sequences. Its story spans galaxies and centuries yet stays focused on hope, loss and love rather than war. Single-player, with full controller support, and suited to players who enjoy emotional, atmospheric adventures.
1676910:
Sound is the terrain in Onde, a calm platformer in which you surf waves made of sound and light through abstract landscapes. By creating fleeting paths to follow, you move through a world that shifts between sharp linework and swirling color, with bursts of crystalline notes, whimsical companions to follow and soothing sound spheres to tune into.

The music adapts as you move, so the soundtrack feels like part of the controls, and the mood is meditative rather than demanding. Movement is fluid and the puzzles are light. Single-player, with full controller support, and suited to players who want a quiet, music-centered experience to wind down with.
1681430:
Patrolling Old Detroit as Alex Murphy, you take the role of the cyborg lawman from the film franchise. RoboCop: Rogue City is a first-person shooter made by Teyon, the studio behind Terminator: Resistance, and it plays as a single-player story.

The game leans on his sturdy armor and signature Auto-9 pistol to make you feel like an unstoppable enforcer, in a setting drawn from the films. Full controller support is included, along with Steam achievements and cloud saves. It suits fans of the movies and anyone who likes shooters built around a strong sense of character.
1693040:
Neon highways inspired by 1980s science fiction set the stage for this arcade racer. At the wheel of a sci-fi supercar, you gather momentum and charge energy while a synthwave soundtrack drives the pace, so music, motion and visuals blend into one continuous run.

Rivals have real physical presence, so they can block overtakes, shove you off your line and cause collisions, which turns every race into a fight for control. Speed is the key resource, so the driving rewards aggression and flow. Single-player, with full controller support, and aimed at arcade racing fans who value atmosphere.
1710540:
Finley is a young pigeon doctor who joins St. Ursula's hospital in a small town named Porcupine. The healthcare system around him is under strain, and he may never reach the work-life balance he hoped for. As seasons turn, you spend time at the hospital, share a beer with villagers at the pub, visit the nearby forest and learn that people are not always honest with themselves or each other.

The world is lovingly illustrated, and the tone is heartfelt rather than action-driven, with darker secrets gradually coming to light. Single-player, with full controller support, and a fit for players who like character-led stories about work, pressure and finding your place.
1726120:
After a freak accident on the verge of winning an international tournament, a golfer lands in Golf Purgatory, and the only way back to the living is to play through its courses. This roguelike golf adventure gives you a limited number of shots to finish each hole within par, and failing sends you back to the start of the course.

Each course is overseen by a spectral Legendary Caddie who teaches the mystical rules of the game, and otherworldly power-ups and wild hazards keep every run unpredictable. It is a demanding single-player game that fuses golf with roguelike structure, best for players who enjoy punishing but replayable action. Full controller support.
1771360:
As the Second World War nears its end in February 1945, the young nurse Gerda Larsen faces a fight of her own: saving her husband Anders after the Gestapo arrests him. She has five days, a community she does not want to abandon and a dangerous world to adapt to. You investigate, explore and decide whom to trust.

This story-rich game uses light role-playing elements. Choices carry both immediate and lasting consequences, from handing out scarce resources to helping someone in pain who may later hurt others. Your personality points and allegiances influence your options. Single-player, with full controller support, it suits players who value moral dilemmas and hard conversations over action.
1796580:
Michelle has been cursed by an archdemon who is looking for love, and she has little time left to break it. This narrative-led survival horror title mixes fixed-camera exploration with first-person shooting in an arcade vein. Her days divide between the dangerous demon world, where her Third Eye lets her see between worlds, and her residential street in a busy London borough.

Inventory and resource management matter, and players can switch to tank controls if they prefer the classic feel. The tone is eccentric and neon-lit, an offbeat take on horror. Single-player, with full controller support, and aimed at fans of retro survival horror who want a stylish twist on the formula.
1815570:
Poker hands are the weapons in Aces & Adventures, a single-player deckbuilding RPG. You assemble a deck that pairs poker hands with ability cards, then fight through a world drawn from Norse and Middle Eastern myth to defend Cardrasil, the Life Tree, against a creeping evil.

There are 13 fully voiced campaigns, plus procedurally generated runs for repeat play, and a mode called the Invernal Spiral that takes inspiration from Slay the Spire and centers on building and managing a deck over a run. You grow stronger and prune your deck as you go. It suits strategy fans who enjoy card games and want a different kind of combat puzzle.
1823930:
Sigrid forms an unlikely friendship with a shadow whose gift lets her run across the surface of the sea. She races across the open water around Strandville, a decaying archipelago and submerged city, and swings between rooftops with her net. Her task is to protect the islanders from sea monsters and confront an old enemy.

The islanders are a varied cast, including fishermen who have had enough and secretive hermits, and Sigrid's cranky grandmother offers help along the way. The story deals with loss and reconciliation, and the surf-style traversal keeps the pace quick. Single-player, with full controller support, and suited to players who like movement-focused adventures with a warm, emotional core.
1903620:
It is 1987 in the small town of Gallows Creek, and a disgraced city DJ named Forrest Nash is hosting a late-night radio show. When a mysterious killer starts stalking callers, the townsfolk turn to him, and you take their calls and puzzle out ways to save each person on the line.

This first-person horror comedy runs on branching conversations with eccentric locals, and decisions come in real time, so every call carries life-and-death stakes. The mix of dread and jokes gives it a lighter tone than most horror. Single-player, with full controller support, and suited to fans of puzzle-driven narrative games who want chills with humor.
1928690:
Armed with a strange teleportation device, a scientist is trying to leave a biomechanical world that is old, hazardous and full of secrets. Bionic Bay is a physics-driven platformer built around a swap ability, which lets you trade places with objects and enemies or shift gravity, using the environment to move, defend and attack.

Realistic physics means fire, ice, breakage and explosions can kill you, so experiments have consequences. The pixel art is dense and gritty, and the sound design builds suspense in each biome. Movement is built with speedrunning in mind. Single-player, with full controller support, and best for players who like precise platforming and creative problem solving.
1939970:
New York, 2329: technology offers eternal life, with consciousness kept in memory banks or moved from body to body for those who can pay. You play Detective James Karra of the Mortality Department, who investigates a case his chief hands him unofficially, with police liaison Sara Kai as his only help.

The case centers on a serial killer picking off members of the elite in the city, and advanced technology helps the pair dig up uncomfortable secrets about the powerful. It is a single-player interactive noir story with a serious, moody tone, aimed at fans of detective fiction and science fiction who like thinking about the cost of immortality. Full controller support is included.
1956040:
You ride a bike around a 1980s town, recruiting friends and neighborhood kids to hold off the Greed, monsters that keep coming for a family relic called Crown of Creation. Along the way you set up defenses, manage a modest base and dig into your family's past.

This is a brief standalone entry in the Kingdom series with a story to follow, built on small-scale strategy and simple controls. You can play solo or share the screen with a second player, and online co-op works through Steam's Remote Play Together feature. A synth-heavy soundtrack and neon colors set the 80s mood.
1975440:
Stan is a professional diver working in the North Sea in an alternate, technologically advanced 1970s. He is coping with a loss that changed his life, and the isolation of long underwater assignments mirrors his state of mind. Strange events begin to unfold beneath the surface as you guide him through his work, and he eventually has to make a major decision.

Grief is the central theme, handled through cinematic visuals and a poetic tone, with the ocean depicted as both beautiful and lonely. This is a single-player narrative adventure with full controller support, suited to players who like emotional, story-led games set deep underwater.
200710:
Loot and constant fighting drive Torchlight II, a dungeon-crawling action RPG whose levels, enemies and treasure are randomized so no two playthroughs match. Beyond the dungeons, an open world offers wide areas to explore. You choose from four classes, each playable as either a male or a female hero with cosmetic customization.

It adds online and LAN co-op to the original's formula, so you can play with friends over the internet or on a local network, with a matchmaking service for finding others. Solo play remains fully viable. Released in 2012, it suits fans of quick, loot-driven dungeon crawling.
202750:
Arizona is the setting for this standalone action-adventure from Remedy, in which the author Alan Wake must stop Mr. Scratch, an evil double who has taken over his life. Combat revolves around fighting with light: you use it to weaken the dark creatures that come at you.

A separate Arcade Mode, Fight till Dawn, challenges you to survive until sunrise and compete against friends on leaderboards. The mix of story and score chasing makes it an easy way in for newcomers as well as returning fans of the series. Single-player, with full controller support.
203350:
Olaf, a young Viking whose father is Tormund the Fierce, leads the defense of the north of Endoria against an undead army spreading toward the kingdom's heart. This tactical RPG is a standalone follow-up to The Legend, set years after that game's events, and it gives him Rune Magic and Valkyries to command.

The campaign takes Olaf across frozen islands, old fortresses and ravaged lands to liberate Nordig. As in the series, you explore the map and fight turn-based battles with an army under your command. It suits strategy-RPG fans who enjoy building an army and growing a hero. Single-player.
204450:
Call of Juarez: Gunslinger frames a first-person shooter as a series of tall tales. Silas Greaves, a bounty hunter in his later years, recounts the outlaws he says he hunted down, and the levels take the player from dusty mining country to saloon interiors. Jesse James, Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid figure among the legends in his account, and the missions revolve around gunfights and quick-draw duels.

The narration is part of the design, because the storyteller's telling shapes what happens on screen. Techland built it as a single-player western with full controller support, aimed at players who want a stylized, violent shooter rooted in Wild West folklore.
2050650:
Six years after Raccoon City, government agent Leon S. Kennedy is sent to a remote European village to find the president's abducted daughter, Ashley, and discovers that the locals are far from normal. This 2023 remake of Capcom's survival horror classic replays that rescue mission with rebuilt visuals, modernized controls and a reworked story. Play is third-person, built around tense gunfights, close-quarters melee and careful management of limited supplies.

The village, its hostile residents and the locations beyond it keep the pressure on throughout. It is a single-player game with full controller support, aimed at horror fans who like action-leaning survival games and at newcomers curious about a modern take on a well-known entry.
205100:
In the industrial whaling city of Dunwall, the Empress's trusted bodyguard is framed for her murder and emerges as a masked assassin intent on revenge. Dishonored is a first-person action game where each mission works like a small sandbox: targets can be approached through shadows, rooftops and back routes, or confronted head-on with blade and pistol. Supernatural powers, including a short-range teleport called Blink, and assorted gadgets widen the options.

How a mission ends depends on the choices made during it. The game is single-player and rewards patience and experimentation, making it a good fit for fans of stealth-minded action and immersive sims who like finding their own route through a level.
205650:
London, 1898: Sherlock Holmes is suspected in a case that mixes theft, fraud and betrayal, and the player leads the investigation. Frogwares' Testament of Sherlock Holmes is an adventure game in which crime scenes are examined, clues gathered, trails followed and suspects questioned until the truth emerges. The Victorian city is presented with an eye to period accuracy, and the plot takes several unexpected turns.

The story leans into a darker side of the detective. The game is single-player and relies on observation and deduction rather than combat, so it suits mystery fans, and readers of the Holmes stories who want a case that puts the great detective under real pressure.
2060870:
Players take the role of Atom Eve, among the strongest heroes in the Invincible universe, in an original story built around her own life. The game follows Eve's daily routine, including her time on the Teen Team and her relationships with relatives and friends, while she looks into a mystery and decides how to use her abilities for good. Everyday problems sit alongside the dangers of being a superhero, and the choices made steer her story.

Rossi Gifford directed the art, and the setting comes from Robert Kirkman's Invincible comic series. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to Invincible readers and anyone who enjoys character-focused, choice-driven storytelling.
207140:
SpeedRunners is a four-player competitive platformer where racing and sabotage happen at once. Each runner sprints, slides and swings on a grappling hook through obstacle-filled courses, and the screen follows the leader, so trailing too far behind means elimination from the round. Rockets, mines and other pick-ups give players ways to hinder their rivals.

Matches can be played locally, online or a mix of both, so two people on a couch can face two others over the internet. The pace is quick, and winning depends on swing timing and sharp reflexes. It suits friends who enjoy competitive party games, and a single-player option is included as well.
20900:
Few choices are clearly right in The Witcher, a single-player RPG set in a grim fantasy world. The player is Geralt of Rivia, a professional monster slayer pulled into a power struggle among rival factions. Quests branch depending on decisions, and consequences often surface long after the choice was made. Characters develop through a large pool of skills, combat styles and magic, and fights unfold in real time with a tactical emphasis.

This Enhanced Edition Director's Cut is a revised release of CD Projekt RED's 2008 original. It is a dialogue-heavy, story-first game, suited to players who prefer moral ambiguity and lasting consequences to fast action.
209190:
Most stealth games ask for patience, but Stealth Bastard Deluxe asks for speed. The player guides a defenseless infiltrator, equipped with nothing but a pair of stealth goggles, through a hostile facility. The character carries no weapons and wears no armor, a single sighting is fatal, and survival depends on staying in shadow and moving between hiding places at the right moments.

Each room works as a compact puzzle of timing and positioning, with traps and patrolling machinery to read and avoid. Deluxe is an expanded version of the original Stealth Bastard. It is a single-player game that suits fans of precise, trial-and-error platformers who like some stealth in the mix.
20920:
With war looming between the northern realms, a conspiracy reaches into the highest circles of power, and Geralt of Rivia, a professional monster hunter, is drawn into the middle of it. The Witcher 2 is a role-playing game with a branching narrative in which decisions carry weight; a major choice partway through sends the story down different paths with different places and allies. Combat is action-oriented and played in real time, supported by alchemy, signs and character progression.

The Enhanced Edition is an updated release of the 2011 game from CD Projekt RED. With a campaign that runs past forty hours, it suits players after a mature, story-heavy single-player RPG in which choices matter.
21000:
After the villains of Arkham Asylum break out together, Batman and Robin take on the job of rounding them up across a brick-built Gotham City. LEGO Batman: The Videogame turns that chase into a lighthearted action adventure, with fights, vehicle sections and small puzzles solved by constructing objects out of bricks and switching between gadgets and suits. Targets include the Joker, the Penguin and the Scarecrow.

A second campaign flips the perspective and lets the player take control of the villains, and two people can play together. The humor and approachable action make it a natural fit for families, younger players and fans of the Dark Knight who enjoy a lighter take on Gotham.
2103680:
Three friends in their early twenties spend a summer in southern Italy, hoping to repair a bond strained by the isolation of the 2020 pandemic. Mediterranea Inferno is a visual novel in which the player chooses how Claudio, Andrea and Mida spend each day, whether lounging by a pool, going out at night or wandering through a cemetery. Every outing exposes more of their insecurities, obsessions and resentments, and the trip drifts toward confrontation.

The tone is tense and adult, with grief, desire and a strained friendship at its core. Its author previously made Milky Way Prince. It is a single-player read for players who want a character-focused, mature narrative rather than gameplay challenge.
210770:
Tower defense meets first-person shooting in Sanctum 2. Each map centers on oxygen-producing Cores that alien waves try to destroy; the player first builds towers to shape the enemy's route, then steps into the fight personally with a weapon when the wave arrives. Four character classes and a loadout system covering towers, weapons and perks allow different approaches to each map.

Because success depends on both layout and aim, the game rewards planning and good shooting in equal measure. It supports single-player and online co-op, where teammates can split the work between building and fighting. It suits strategy players who want more hands-on action, and shooter fans who enjoy designing a defense.
2111090:
Minesweeper-style tile flipping drives this roguelite puzzle game set in the land of Beebom. The player hunts a tyrannical King across procedurally generated maze maps, turning over tiles and working out where the King's henchmen are hiding. Those henchmen can be dodged or fought in turn-based encounters, and over a hundred items and abilities gathered along the way change the approach before a final showdown in Beebom City.

Hand-animated art from the animation studio BUCK and an original score by Antfood give Let's! Revolution! a distinctive look and sound. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits puzzle fans who enjoy deduction, especially those drawn to replayable roguelite runs.
212030:
Drawing on old Chinese revenge stories, Kung Fu Strike - The Warrior's Rise is an arcade-style beat-'em-up spread over 28 stages. The player fights through opponents with punches, kicks and timed blocks, linking moves into long combos. Items and abilities unlocked along the way change how the fighter plays, and online leaderboards compare scores with other players.

A second player can join through local co-op or fight against the first. Later stages stay demanding even at the lowest difficulty, so it suits players who like old-school brawlers and score chasing and are willing to learn the combat system properly.
214170:
Rivellon faces a threat from a cult called the Black Ring, which is trying to bring the Lord of Chaos into the world, and Divine Divinity makes the player the prophesied Chosen One expected to stop it. Guided by the wizard Zandalor, the player must rally the seven peoples of the land. Larian Studios pairs real-time hack-and-slash combat with a large explorable world, plenty of items to find and trade, and a broad set of skills to grow into.

As the first game in what became the Divinity series, it is a long single-player adventure, billed as lasting more than a hundred hours. It suits fans of classic, exploration-heavy RPGs.
214340:
Rufus, a scheming inventor from the lowest social class, is stuck on Deponia, a world buried in rubbish, and dreams of escaping to Elysium, the floating city of the wealthy. When a woman named Goal drops from above into his trash pile, he sees a way up and sets out to return her, kicking off a string of ill-advised plans. The game is a comedy adventure with a love story at its center.

Play follows the point-and-click tradition: explore hand-drawn scenes, collect items and combine them to get past absurd obstacles. The humor is sarcastic and the lead a self-serving anti-hero, so it suits fans of classic LucasArts-style comedy adventures. It is single-player.
2147330:
Iris is a reflection with a sarcastic streak, living in a mirror world that resembles ours but differs in small ways. Still Joking is a narrative adventure that blends visual novel and interactive fiction, following her as she investigates the death of the person she mirrors while working out where she belongs. The culprit is known early, so the investigation is about motive.

The story is long and text-heavy, with more than a thousand choices, roughly twelve to fifteen hours of reading and several endings for the main storylines and individual characters. Interactive points, quick-time events and investigation mechanics break up the reading, and a fully voiced cat adds personality. It suits readers of long, choice-driven mysteries.
214770:
Wrestling moves double as both weapons and keys in Guacamelee! Gold Edition, an exploration-driven platformer in the Metroidvania mold, set in a world drawn from Mexican culture and folklore. The hero is a luchador, and moves such as the Rooster Uppercut serve in combat and also for reaching new places, so fighting and platforming feed into each other. A dimension-swap mechanic shifts the world between two states, revealing hidden areas that are otherwise unreachable.

A second player can join in local co-op, and the Gold Edition is a fuller release of the game. It suits fans of Metroidvanias and melee brawlers who enjoy colorful, folklore-inspired settings and are happy to backtrack as new abilities unlock.
2161620:
Time rewinding is the core trick of Lysfanga: The Time Shift Warrior, a tactical action game starring Ime, a protector of the kingdom of Antala who has been granted temporal powers by the Goddess of Time. Rewinding during combat summons clones of her earlier selves to fight beside her, turning one warrior into a small army against the Raxes, demons that have escaped from ancient cities.

Moving through those cities unlocks additional weapons and spells for facing a larger threat. Planning how and when to use the clones matters as much as quick reactions. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who enjoy action games with a tactical, puzzle-like layer.
216910:
Fantasy's usual order is turned around in Of Orcs And Men: the Empire of Men persecutes, enslaves and massacres the Orcs and Goblins, and the player sides with the hunted. The player directs two heroes, a powerful Orc fighter and a Goblin who specializes in stealth and assassination. Their mission takes them deep into enemy territory with a single goal, killing the Emperor.

Characters gain levels and learn new abilities, with the pair covering brute force and quiet killing between them. It is a single-player action RPG with full controller support, built on a premise of persecution and revolt. The Goblin, Styx, later got a game of his own from Cyanide.
218680:
Writing a word makes it real in Scribblenauts Unlimited, a puzzle-adventure in which the player types the name of an object and it appears. As Maxwell, the player explores free-roaming, connected areas and helps the residents with their problems, choosing whichever item, creature or tool seems suited to the situation. Because the solutions are open-ended, many puzzles accept several answers.

An object creator lets players design their own items, assign properties to them and share them through Steam Workshop. The story digs into Maxwell's family, including his siblings and how he came to own his magical notepad. Single-player and open-ended, it suits creative players who enjoy experimenting.
219910:
At a strict convent school, quiet and obedient Lilli copes with Mother Superior's harsh rule by retreating into her imagination. When her friend Edna vanishes under unexplained circumstances, Lilli sets out to find her in Edna & Harvey: Harvey's New Eyes, a point-and-click adventure, and the search forces her to face her own subconscious fears.

The tone mixes dark comedy with unease, anchored by a protagonist whose politeness covers something stranger. Puzzles follow the genre's inventory-and-dialogue logic. Made by Daedalic, the studio behind Deponia and The Whispered World, it is single-player and suits adventure fans who want a macabre, offbeat story over a lighthearted one.
22300:
You grow up in underground Vault 101 and set out after your father abruptly departs, stepping into a ruined Washington, D.C. region about two centuries after nuclear war. Super mutants, radiation and wild creatures make the surface dangerous, but the map is open, so you can follow the main story or wander toward quests and ruins of your own choosing.

Combat runs in real time, with the option to pause and target body parts using V.A.T.S., and your choices shape how characters treat you. The tone mixes bleak survival with dark humor. It is a single-player role-playing game for people who like exploring and building a character through a seven-attribute stat system.
223470:
A single week of errands keeps spiraling into chaos for a hapless everyman known as the Postal Dude. POSTAL 2 is a first-person comedy-action game set in open environments full of caricatured townspeople, a toy mascot gone bad named Krotchy, a besieged religious compound run by Uncle Dave and a not entirely loyal pit bull named Champ. Weapons range from a plain shovel to heavier firepower, and the AI reacts in unpredictable ways to what the player does.

The humor is crude, violent and deliberately offensive, aimed at an adult audience comfortable with that. Players can approach the errands in different ways. It is single-player with full controller support.
223730:
Across more than forty levels, Fly'N mixes platforming and puzzle-solving in a lush, colorful world. The player guides four small creatures called Buds, each with a different power, as they try to protect the World-Trees from the villain Dyer, a hair-dryer bent on wrecking their Helys. Progress depends on working out which combination of abilities suits each hazard, and on moving Helys around and using the scenery to liberate Helicia's inhabitants.

The tone is light and the visuals are charming, with a mix of action and thinking. It is a single-player game suited to players who like puzzle platformers and enjoy experimenting to find what works.
228260:
Rebuilding after a magical Cataclysm is the task in Fallen Enchantress: Legendary Heroes, a turn-based fantasy 4X game set in the world of Elemental. The player grows a single settlement into an empire by founding cities, training armies and expanding, while quests and monsters such as liches and banshees press in from outside. Champions are drawn to the ruler according to the fame the realm has earned, and the sovereign and champions develop along skill trees.

Because each game plays out differently, campaigns differ on replay. It is a single-player strategy game from Stardock, the company behind Galactic Civilizations. It fits 4X fans who like role-playing elements, such as heroes and quests, added to empire building.
2290180:
Biking, skiing, snowboarding and wingsuit flying share one enormous map in Riders Republic, an open-world sports game built from urban streets and several U.S. national parks, among them Yosemite, Zion and the Grand Canyon. Players can switch between disciplines on the fly and take part in races, trick competitions and relaxed group rides alongside other riders online.

Large-scale races field more than fifty participants, and seasonal events add new sports and challenges over time. Cosmetic unlocks allow players to customize their rider's look. The game supports solo play, co-op and PvP, and it suits people who enjoy extreme sports and want variety in what they ride and how they compete.
230820:
Jerry Hazelnut wants to become a magician. When a talking white rabbit offers him an apprenticeship, he follows it to Mousewood, a woodland world of animal villagers and old secrets. You solve puzzles, trade conversation and gather items in a classic point-and-click adventure, learning spells along the way.

The story moves between cozy humor and something creepier as a threat settles over the forest and the people living in it. It is a fairy-tale adventure from Daedalic Entertainment, single-player, with full controller support.
