Fans of storybook settings with a darker streak and traditional adventure puzzles will feel at home here.
234270:
This adventure retells Ken Follett's novel about a cathedral being raised in twelfth-century England. You take turns as Philip, Jack and Aliena, three people whose paths cross in the town of Kingsbridge while hardship and conflict press in on them. Exploring, talking and making decisions lets you alter how events from the book play out.

The pace is unhurried and driven by story, closer to an interactive novel than an action game. Conversation and choices matter more than quick reactions. Readers of the book and fans of narrative adventures are the natural audience. It is a single-player game with full controller support.
235540:
Ubersreik has been overrun by Skaven, the rat-men of the Warhammer Fantasy setting, and Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide has a team of up to four heroes fight through the swarm across a series of missions. It is a cooperative action game combining first-person melee and ranged combat, with locations ranging from the heights of Magnus Tower to the Under Empire below. Players choose from five heroes, each with different abilities, gear and personality.

Teamwork is central, since the swarms punish players who stray from the group. Friends can join online, and AI companions can fill empty slots. It suits fans of cooperative horde games who prefer melee-heavy combat to long-range shooting.
236730:
Tower defense is flipped around in Anomaly 2: rather than building turrets, the player leads a convoy of vehicles through machine-held territory and has to get it past the enemy's guns. The sequel moves the action to a frozen, post-apocalyptic Earth, where surviving humans travel in convoys searching for supplies, and the player's own convoy is called Yukon. Units can morph between forms, which adds flexibility to how a squad is arranged and used.

Besides the single-player campaign, a multiplayer mode pits tower defense against tower offense, with one side defending while the other attacks. The game follows Anomaly Warzone Earth and suits strategy fans who want a tactical twist on a familiar genre.
236850:
Four centuries of history are open to the player in Europa Universalis IV, a grand strategy game that begins in the closing years of the Middle Ages and runs to the Napoleonic era. Every nation on the map can be led, and the daily work involves diplomacy, war, trade, exploration and economic management in pursuit of wealth, territory and prestige. The clock runs continuously but can be paused, so decisions pile up quickly.

This edition is packaged with its base game, three expansions and a cosmetic pack. Both single-player and multiplayer are supported, including co-op and PvP. It suits players who enjoy a deep, historically grounded sandbox and are prepared to learn a complex set of systems.
238010:
Adam Jensen, a former SWAT specialist, works security for a biotechnology company until armed attackers raid the facility and kill the scientists he was hired to protect. Deus Ex: Human Revolution casts the player as Jensen, rebuilt with mechanical augmentations and drawn into a conspiracy across a near-future world split between people who can afford such upgrades and those who cannot.

Levels leave room for different approaches, including stealth, direct combat, hacking and conversation, and the game mixes action with role-playing progression. This Director's Cut is a revised edition of the original. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits fans of immersive sims who like to choose how a problem gets solved.
238320:
Armed with nothing but a camcorder, independent journalist Miles Upshur sneaks into Mount Massive Asylum in the Colorado mountains after receiving a tip about the Murkoff Corporation's secretive operations there. Outlast is survival horror from a first-person view, and the building turns out to be overrun by dangerous patients and something worse. The camcorder's night vision makes dark corridors navigable but drains batteries that must be found as the player goes.

There is no combat; encounters are about evasion, hiding in lockers and fleeing through vents. It is a single-player game with full controller support, intended for horror fans comfortable with intense, helpless tension and graphic content.
239140:
Harran, a quarantined city devastated by a viral outbreak, is the setting of Dying Light, a first-person survival game in an open world. The player scavenges for supplies, crafts and repairs melee weapons, and uses parkour-style movement across rooftops to travel and escape. The day-night cycle changes the danger: daytime favors gathering and completing quests, while night brings faster, more aggressive threats.

It can be played alone or in online co-op, and a PvP mode is available. The Essentials Edition packages the base game with several add-ons, and the free Retouched Update revises the visuals and soundtrack for all owners. It suits players who like survival games built around mobility as much as combat.
2396240:
Captain Leeway and a crew of steam-powered robots travel the seas by submarine to investigate a water crisis that has turned deadly for metal bodies. SteamWorld Heist II is a turn-based tactics game in which aiming is done by hand: during missions the player positions the crew, lines up shots and bounces bullets off walls to hit enemies behind cover. Travel between missions includes real-time battles at sea.

More than 150 items allow crews to be customized, and the adventure runs over thirty hours. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to tactics fans who like precision aiming and trick shots as much as planning.
241910:
Rufus is back with another scheme to escape his junk-covered home planet in Goodbye Deponia, the third game in the Deponia series and a point-and-click comedy. The Organon, which plans to destroy Deponia, is moving ahead, Goal has disappeared again, and Rufus is convinced he has finally found a flawless plan for reaching Elysium, the paradise above. Events refuse to cooperate, and this time three versions of Rufus are causing trouble at once.

Puzzles combine inventory items and conversation, with the same sarcastic, slapstick humor as before. Newcomers will be better served by starting earlier in the series. It is single-player, aimed at adventure fans who enjoy absurd comedy and long chains of puzzle logic.
242110:
Stuntman Joe Danger returns for a run through the sets of a blockbuster movie in Joe Danger 2: The Movie, a side-scrolling stunt-racing game spread over 100 levels. Each setting changes the vehicle and the challenge, whether a police motorcycle, a jetpack, a minecart, a quad bike or a unicycle, and the player pulls off tricks and gets past obstacles on the way.

A Movie Maker tool lets players build their own levels and swap them through Steam Workshop. The game supports controller or keyboard and mouse, and it includes a multiplayer option. It suits players who enjoy bright, arcade-style stunt platformers and like making and trading their own courses.
242640:
Two centuries old and thoroughly sarcastic, the Goblin Styx stars in Styx: Master of Shadows, a stealth game with role-playing progression set in a dark fantasy world. He has made his way into the enormous Tower of Akenash, home of the World-Tree and its magical Amber sap, hoping to learn about his origins and profit along the way. Missions involve getting past guards unseen, recovering information and eliminating targets, either with quiet kills or by staging accidents.

Amber-based abilities, such as invisibility or a decoy clone, complement skills unlocked through experience. The tower's vertical layout encourages searching for alternate routes. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to stealth fans who enjoy sneaking and planning.
243450:
The city is the course in Urban Trial Freestyle, a trials-bike game where riders tackle obstacles in urban settings, chaining tricks such as backflips, 360s and wallrides. Modes include Time Attack, Stunt and Challenges across five different environments, and bike and rider customization lets players tune a setup for speed or for style.

Ghost Mode allows racing against other riders' recorded runs, and over 140 online leaderboards keep score comparisons going. Physics-driven handling rewards practice, and the retry-and-improve loop is the heart of the game. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who enjoy trials games and chasing a cleaner, faster run.
243950:
Three styles of play meet in Divinity: Dragon Commander, a strategy game with role-playing elements. On a turn-based campaign map the player manages an empire, makes political decisions as an aspiring emperor and positions armies; battles then play out in real time on land, sea and air. During those fights the ruler can take dragon form to join the action personally and support the troops.

The result blends governing, role-playing and real-time tactics. Larian Studios developed it, and it includes both single-player and multiplayer. It suits strategy players who want a mix of governance, tactics and direct action rather than a single narrow RTS loop.
244160:
Fleet command in three-dimensional space is the focus of the Homeworld Remastered Collection, which packages Homeworld and Homeworld 2 as updated real-time strategy games along with remastered multiplayer, plus the original versions as a bonus. Players gather resources, research technology and build ships from small fighters up to large carriers, then choose formations and tactics for each mission. More than thirty single-player missions are included across the campaigns.

Because battles take place in full 3D, positioning and approach angle matter more than they do in typical ground-based RTS games. People from the original development team contributed to the remasters. The collection suits strategy fans who want a campaign-driven space fleet game with room to plan.
247080:
Every step and swing must land on the beat in Crypt of the NecroDancer, a roguelike dungeon crawler built as a rhythm game. Enemies move to the music as well, so the player reads their patterns while descending through ever-changing floors, fighting skeletons, zombies, dragons and other creatures. The soundtrack was composed by Danny Baranowsky, and players can load songs from their own MP3 collection to set the rhythm.

Fifteen playable characters offer different play styles, and the game works with a keyboard, a controller or a USB dance pad. Local co-op supports a second player, and mod support is included. It suits fans of roguelikes and rhythm games who enjoy tight, pattern-based challenge.
247430:
Framed as memories of earlier jobs, Hitman: Contracts follows Agent 47 through a series of assassinations in a stealth-action game. Each level hands the player a target or two and plenty of freedom in how to reach them: picking up disguises to move through restricted areas, improvising weapons from the surroundings, or taking a more direct route when the situation allows. Locations span the globe, and the people on the hit list are terrorists and crime bosses.

Enemy guards operate in squads rather than alone, which raises the cost of being spotted. The game is single-player and fits fans of open-ended stealth puzzles who want an earlier chapter in the series from Io-Interactive.
2482760:
Wilderness in Colorado and Texas is the setting for Hunting Simulator 3, an open-world hunting game played on foot or from an all-terrain vehicle. Each region holds dozens of wild species, and a system called SimFauna governs their behavior: animals react to what the hunter does and age over time. A trained dog helps in the field, and licensed gear from real brands such as Remington and Browning covers firearms, bows and crossbows.

The loop centers on tracking animals, choosing equipment and taking considered shots. The game is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who enjoy hunting and outdoors simulation and want a large map to explore at their own pace.
24880:
Nazi-occupied Paris in the 1940s is the backdrop for The Saboteur, an open-world action game starring Sean Devlin, an Irish racecar mechanic who joins the French Resistance to get revenge on Colonel Kurt Dierker, the officer who executed his best friend. Missions mix gunfights, stealth, disguises and driving, with sabotage targets such as trains, bridges and enemy facilities, and landmarks like the Eiffel Tower and Notre Dame can be climbed.

The city's color is drained in areas under heavy occupation and returns as the Resistance regains ground, giving it a distinctive look. It is a single-player game suited to players who want pulpy, World War II-set open-world action rather than a realistic war simulation.
252130:
The Grim Reaper wants friends, and since only the dead will keep him company, he floods the land and strands a flock of sheep on tiny islands. You rescue them by solving math puzzles built on adding and subtracting sheep, including slicing them in half with lasers.

There are 120 puzzles across four worlds, starting gently and growing steadily harder. The humor turns dark as it goes, so it is not meant for young children despite the cute premise. Wolves and a kraken add hazards along the way. It suits single-player puzzle fans who like number logic and macabre comedy.
252750:
Schrodinger, a cat scientist, is building a machine powered by mice, and you help him by guiding the mice from the start of each level to the exit. They walk on their own, so you drop Tetris-style blocks to form bridges and safe routes across gaps and hazards, while also collecting items, fighting enemies and blowing things up.

The game blends falling-block pieces with Lemmings-style rescue across 80 handcrafted levels. Different block types and environmental dangers keep each puzzle distinct, and the aim is to bring home the largest number of mice you can. It is single-player with full controller support, aimed at players who like spatial planning with some action mixed in.
254840:
In the year 2741, the Terran Empire is besieging a coalition of colonies called the Northern Star Alliance, which stands for freedom and democracy. Pushed out of space, the Alliance holds one last stronghold. You command squads of vehicles and troops in real-time battles across a campaign covering two factions and 24 missions.

The game centers on controlling squads on the battlefield, which gives the strategy an action-leaning feel. The campaign supports co-op for up to three players in total, and drop-in competitive multiplayer supports as many as eight. It suits strategy fans who enjoy directing a limited force in the field.
254880:
Set in a future where Earth's resources have run low and alliances between nations are fraying, this turn-based game hands you command of a lunar territory. You locate and tap energy pools to take out rival factions, while protecting your own base with shields, surveillance and weapons.

It is easy to learn but hard to master, with several distinct opposing factions, bright graphics and customizable terrains. You can play against the computer or against friends, so it works for solo sessions or head-to-head matches. It comes from Humongous Entertainment and suits players who enjoy methodical tactical play.
256330:
The official game of the 2013 World Rally Championship season puts you through a career mode featuring the drivers, cars and routes of the WRC, WRC 2 and WRC 3 classes, with the Junior WRC class appearing in the series for the first time.

The game offers 78 courses across 13 countries and 65 official cars, with varied weather and road surfaces that change how the car handles. Online multiplayer supports up to 16 players. It suits racing fans who want a licensed rally season to work through, with options for both solo play and online competition.
25900:
Taking the role of a treasure hunter for the crown, you head to the land of Endoria looking for riches and old secrets. You travel between towns, wilderness and dungeons in real time, then fight turn-based battles with an army you recruit and manage along the way.

Fights hinge on where units stand, how morale shifts, which creatures fill your army and how you use spells, so preparation counts for more than reflexes. The story starts simply and grows into a tale with twists and a memorable ending. As an early entry in the modern King's Bounty line, it suits single-player fans of fantasy tactics who like thinking through each fight.
260160:
Koru is a young boy in Colortown, a city built on creativity and emotion, where a dark force called the Bleakness is draining color and joy from the world. You guide him through a 3D action adventure, using color and emotion to bring the city back to life. Despite a style that recalls 1990s mascot platformers, the game has no jump button at all.

Developer Mimimi Games cites Jak and Daxter and Banjo-Kazooie as touchstones, and the tone is bright, colorful and family-friendly. It is a single-player game with full controller support that works for playing alongside children or for adults who want a lighthearted throwback.
2610650:
Standing still is a bad idea in this Y2K-styled arena movement shooter. You fight through robot drones sent by the mining corporation Tigris Nix, which wants to drain a natural force called the Love from your planet. Destroying its drones helps heal the Oasis.

Speed is the core mechanic, and moving fast is rewarded twice, since it raises both your damage and your healing. Wave hopping, dashes, double jumps and ground slams carry the movement, while weapons with secondary fire modes combine for layered effects and bigger Love scores. It draws on boomer shooters and suits single-player fans of fast, precise, high-skill shooting.
261110:
Designer Suda51 is behind this stylish action game, which casts you as Mondo Zappa, a suave executioner who takes on his targets by slicing and shooting, with a mix of love and killing running through the story.

This PC edition adds a Nightmare difficulty in which enemies fall only to Adrenaline Burst, Dodge Burst or headshots, and the quick-time-event finishers are disabled, so fights call for sharper tactics. A Theater Mode lets you rewatch cutscenes with extra character background after your first playthrough. Single-player with full controller support, it suits action fans who enjoy a stylized, demanding game.
261470:
Galaxies in this real-time 4X game set in space can hold up to 1,400 star systems and as many as 50,000 bodies, from planets to asteroids. You can pause at any moment while you explore, expand, research, trade and fight to build an empire among them.

Universe is the collector's edition, gathering the earlier Distant Worlds releases in one package with a new storyline, an updated manual and expanded modding support. The pausable design aims to pair the depth of turn-based strategy with simpler real-time control. Single-player only, it suits players who enjoy managing a sprawling empire at a large, detailed scale.
266510:
Each quest begins in a remote cabin, where a mysterious dealer lays out cards and you draw them to learn which encounters, choices and rewards lie ahead. When a card leads to a fight, the game switches to real-time third-person combat, making it part card game and part action RPG.

You earn new cards by completing quests and choose which ones go into your deck, which shapes the encounters you face. Quests can be replayed with different draws, so it suits players who like the unpredictability of tabletop adventure books combined with hack-and-slash action. Single-player with full controller support.
269710:
Story mode and competitive multiplayer share the stage in this action-puzzle game. In the story campaign, puzzles grow steadily more inventive while you assist a sausage in making friends and uncover the fate of the Tumblecrown.

Up to four players can compete on a single computer, and online play includes ranked matchmaking for racing friends or new opponents. Computer-controlled bots can fill open slots, with a punishing Nightmare bot for those who want a real test. The story campaign runs past 40 hours. Full controller support is included, and it suits puzzle fans who like both solo challenge and rivalry.
274350:
His name ruined by a deadly circus fire, Dropsy the clown travels a detailed, colorful world to help people in need, uncover dark secrets and, above all, hand out hugs. His father is gravely ill, most people have turned away from him, and he can talk to animals.

This is a point-and-click adventure with an unconventional approach, built around kindness. Players choose whom to help and in what order instead of following a single fixed path. The story deals with love and undeserved kindness. It is a single-player game for adventure fans who like offbeat, bittersweet storytelling.
274520:
Survival horror gets a top-down treatment in Darkwood, set in a ruined, mysterious forest. By day you explore the changing landscape and scavenge for supplies; by night you retreat to a hideout, reinforce it and wait for dawn.

You travel between hideouts across several dense biomes, collecting resources, allies and information as you go. The locals offer dark quests and rewards, and the story shifts depending on the choices you make. It is a slow, tense single-player experience for horror fans who enjoy scarcity and uncertainty. Full controller support is included.
276810:
Based on the Games Workshop tabletop game of the same name, this is a turn-based tactics title set in a ruined Empire city in the Warhammer setting. You lead a warband through lethal skirmishes against rival groups, all hunting for fragments of Wyrdstone left behind when a comet struck the city.

Campaigns combine RPG progression with detailed unit customization, so your fighters gain skills and gear over time. Playable warbands include the Sisters of Sigmar. Battles are fast and unforgiving, and you can play the single-player campaign or take on other players online. It suits tactics fans who accept that units will be lost.
2800:
You play Julian Gardna, continuing the story begun in X: Beyond the Frontier, in a space simulator where you fly between sectors, mine asteroids for materials and sell them on. The universe holds more than 130 sectors, some filled with nebulas that interfere with ships and stations.

More than 60 ships range from small scouts to large carrier-class vessels, and upgrades can be installed, including ones that use a scripting engine built for the game. Redesigned ships and stations and a refreshed graphics engine update the look of the series. This 2006 release is single-player and suits players who like open-ended trading and exploration.
2810:
Following X2: The Threat, this sequel brings a new 3D engine, a new story and new ships to the space trading and combat series. You fly freely through a large universe, trading goods, fighting and building up an empire of your own.

The economy is more complex than in earlier games: computer-controlled characters build factories and trade on their own, wars can shift the global economy, and pirates behave more realistically. An Artificial Life system is meant to keep the universe evolving, so the player's actions can influence it. It is a single-player game for those who enjoy deep space-trading simulation and are happy to set their own goals.
281610:
Set before the original Homeworld games, this ground-based real-time strategy game sends you across the dunes of Kharak at the head of a fleet of ground and air vehicles. The campaign follows Rachel S'jet, who guides her people through an expedition sparked by an anomaly in the southern desert.

Developer Blackbird Interactive was formed by Homeworld veterans along with people who worked on Company of Heroes. Its vehicles run from small, agile attack units to heavier machines. The game offers a single-player campaign and multiplayer, and suits strategy fans who like origin stories and vehicle-based combat.
282070:
Civilians, not soldiers, are the focus here. You manage a small group sheltering in a besieged city, scavenging for what they need while hunger, illness, snipers and hostile scavengers threaten them.

The Final Cut edition collects every update and free expansion to date, remasters the classic locations and adds a new scenario with a new character, plus extra quests and locations drawn from the Stories DLC. It is a somber single-player survival game in which choices are rarely clean, aimed at players who want to see war from the civilian side.
286690:
In 2033, an apocalyptic event has left the surface toxic and barren, and the remnants of humanity shelter in the Moscow Metro, where stations have become besieged city-states. You play Artyom, raised underground, who sets out on a dangerous trip to the center of the tunnel network to warn the others of a coming threat.

This Redux edition is a remastered release of the original first-person shooter, with mutants and rival factions waiting along the route. Ammunition is scarce, and the tone is tense and atmospheric. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to fans of story-driven post-apocalyptic action.
289070:
Lead a civilization from its first settlement toward one of five kinds of victory in this turn-based strategy game. Cities spread across the map, with districts, wonders and improvements each placed on separate hexes, so you choose which specializations to develop.

Research into technology and culture opens up new possibilities, and rival leaders pursue agendas shaped by their historical traits, so each opponent plays a little differently. You can play solo or against other players online. It suits strategy fans who enjoy long campaigns and shaping an empire's layout turn by turn.
289520:
Villains take the lead in this standalone King's Bounty entry, which turns the usual fantasy setup on its head. You choose from three dark heroes, a demoness, a vampire lord or an orc warlord, each with its own opening situation, individual story and way of playing.

The world is large and hostile, with towns, wilderness and dungeons full of quests and secrets, and the familiar forces of light stand against you. You build an army and settle fights in turn-based battle, often facing morally dark choices along the way. It suits single-player fans of fantasy tactics who would like to play the other side.
290300:
At the frontier of explored space, you captain a powerful star destroyer and decide what kind of spacefarer to be. You battle pirates, mine asteroids, scavenge wreckage, trade goods, investigate anomalies and deal with some outlandish aliens.

Playing as a do-gooder, a trader or a privateer, or a mix of all three, you earn credits to buy bigger ships and fit them with weapons and defenses. Ship combat has a naval flavor, and the tone is playful and swashbuckling. It is a single-player space adventure with full controller support, suited to players who like open-ended combat and trading.
2909400:
Cloud and his companions leave Midgar behind and head across the wider world in this second part of the three-game remake of Final Fantasy VII. You explore a large open world, gallop over grasslands on a chocobo and follow the story as the Shinra company keeps draining the planet's lifestream.

Combat blends real-time action with menu-driven commands. The PC release adds options such as NVIDIA DLSS, variable refresh rate and DualSense controller support. It is a single-player game with full controller support, best suited to RPG fans following the remake trilogy.
292030:
Geralt of Rivia, a monster slayer for hire, travels a sprawling, grim fantasy world in search of his adopted daughter Ciri. Contracts, side quests and story missions lead him through villages, cities and wild country, with monsters to hunt and choices to make along the way.

This remastered version updates the RPG with a set of upgrades and enhancements. Your decisions shape how quests turn out, and combat mixes swordplay, signs and potions. It is a single-player game suited to RPG fans who enjoy a large, story-heavy world with plenty to do away from the main plot.
294750:
The roles are reversed in the final game of the Anomaly series. Earlier titles had you leading humans against alien invaders; here you defend the alien homeworld against a human counterattack.

Tower defense moves quickly here: enemy soldiers shoot back at your towers, so you need to watch the battlefield and counterattack. Eight upgradable towers come with special abilities such as repairs, berserk mode and sacrificial explosions, and at the start of each campaign you tailor the tech tree to your needs. Developed by 11 bit studios, it is a single-player game for tower defense fans who like to stay busy.
296910:
Out of work and feeling low, the title character remembers the 8-bit console of his childhood and the games he loved on it. The result is a tribute to the platformers of the 1980s and 1990s, built around classic running and jumping, power-ups, coin collecting and boss battles.

The game has 56 levels across five worlds, hidden warp zones and more than 300 secret locations to find. The main story runs roughly 8 to 12 hours. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to platformer fans who like old-school design and hunting for secrets.
301640:
World War II is ending, and Hitler has unleashed one last gamble in the form of undead super soldiers spreading across Europe. You fight through three campaigns and 15 missions of third-person shooting, alone or with others, in a pulpy horror tone.

The package contains remastered versions of Nazi Zombie Army and Nazi Zombie Army 2 along with a new third chapter and a horde mode. It also adds the eight survivors from Left 4 Dead. Cooperative play is a central draw, and the game also works solo, so it suits shooter fans who like fighting off undead waves with friends.
301650:
First-person vehicle combat meets real-time strategy in this remaster of the 1998 sci-fi game. It is set in an alternate 1960s where the American and Soviet space programs conceal a war fought across the solar system over a strange alien resource called bio-metal.

You scavenge bio-metal, build facilities, set up defenses and command an army of tanks, cruisers and other vehicles on battlefields from the Moon to Titan. Redux brings updated visuals, online multiplayer and Steam Workshop mod support. It suits fans of hybrid action-strategy who want a Cold War-flavored sci-fi setting.
304430:
Playdead's side-scrolling platformer follows a boy who is hunted and alone as he is drawn toward the center of a sinister project. You run, hide and work through environmental puzzles, with danger never far behind, and the story unfolds without any spoken dialogue.

Its look is moody, its soundtrack ambient and its atmosphere unsettling. It pairs tension with puzzles that ask for careful thought, and it is single-player with full controller support. It suits players who like tense, atmospheric, narrative-driven platforming and are comfortable with a dark tone.
307670:
Warren's life is upended by tragedy, and his quest for revenge drags him into a supernatural version of the Wild West, where he hunts down everyone who wronged him. Dark pacts with powers beyond comprehension carry lasting consequences for the people around him.

Hard West is a turn-based tactics game with eight story-driven scenarios and 40 individually designed combat missions. A varied cast of playable characters have fates tied to yours, and hard choices shape the outcome. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to tactics fans who like a Western with an occult streak.
307960:
Flying a World War II aircraft over Stalingrad is the heart of this combat flight simulation, the latest in the long-running IL-2 Sturmovik series. A single-player Career mode puts you in the role of a combat pilot and can be played across the Stalingrad, Moscow and Kuban theatres you own.

The simulation aims for more realistic aerodynamics and physics than earlier entries, at a larger scale. Co-op and online PvP modes are included, and VR is supported. It suits dedicated flight sim fans who want an accurate recreation of wartime air battles.
310510:
Strongholds built long ago to keep otherworldly monsters at bay are under attack again as creatures pour back into the world. You pick a hero and defend the forts by using, rebuilding and upgrading old traps and magical contraptions.

The game mixes tower defense with action RPG elements, so you fight on the battlefield alongside your traps instead of only placing them. Whirling blades, deadly machines and plenty of gore set the tone. The single-player campaign is the centerpiece, with multiplayer also supported and full controller support. It suits tower defense fans who want to be in the thick of the fight.
312660:
Karl Fairburne is back in this third-person tactical shooter set in wartime Italy, where he works to liberate the country from Fascist control. The story takes place after Sniper Elite 3, and levels run from sunny coastal towns to forests, mountain valleys and huge Nazi installations.

The levels are large and give you several ways to approach each objective, with long-range shots central to the combat. It supports single-player, co-op and multiplayer, and has full controller support. It suits patient players who like planning an approach and picking their moment.
312670:
Egypt in the 1930s is the backdrop, and the witch queen Seteki has returned after 4,000 years underground. A team of daring adventurers, the Strange Brigade, is all that stands in her way.

This third-person shooter mixes blasting mummified and undead enemies with exploring ruins, solving puzzles and dodging traps, all in a pulpy, playful adventure tone. You can play alone or team up with up to three others in online co-op. It has full controller support and suits friends who want a lighthearted undead-shooting adventure.
316790:
Manny Calavera works as a travel agent for the Department of Death, selling packages to souls on the four-year trek to eternal rest. When a conspiracy starts to threaten his own salvation, he has to untangle the plot against him in the afterlife.

This adventure game blends film noir with Mexican folklore, and it has been remastered with improved visuals, sound and controls compared with the original release. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to fans of classic adventure games who like puzzles, memorable characters and offbeat storytelling.
3170:
Playing Princess Amelie, you lead an army across Teana, searching for a legendary knight named Bill Gilbert. You explore a large hand-built world map, recruit creatures to your side, and fight turn-based battles in which each unit's position and abilities matter.

Each region brings tougher enemies and bigger rewards, with powerful bosses and a new race of Lizards among the foes. The game continues from the earlier King's Bounty: The Legend with deeper tactics, so it suits fans of turn-based strategy and role-playing who like planning army builds and adapting to new threats. It is single-player.
319050:
Julian Gollop, designer of the original XCOM, is behind this turn-based wizard duelling game that mixes chess-like positioning with poker-style bluffing. Between two and six players duel in arenas using a deck of spells and summoned creatures such as the Gooey Blob and Shadow Wood.

Single-player Realm Quests send you up against Kings and Wizard Lords, and you can also bring others into co-op battles or invade another player's realm. Online options include monthly leagues and both live and asynchronous matches. With wizard customization and a large pool of gear, it suits tactics fans who enjoy unpredictability and mind games.
320300:
Customers bring cars into your workshop with faults to find and fix, and you diagnose and repair them with your tools, earning money to expand the garage and sharpen your skills. It is a hands-on take on the daily routine of a car mechanic.

You can also pick up neglected cars, fix them up and resell them at a profit, or build a collection. This edition adds new cars, tools, options and parts compared with the earlier version. It is a single-player management simulation that suits players who enjoy methodical tinkering and growing a small business at their own pace.
322190:
Steam-powered robot pirates are your crew, and you board enemy spaceships to loot and fight in tactical shootouts. It is turn-based strategy, but you aim each shot yourself, which allows skill shots and ricochets off walls.

Levels are procedurally generated, and you upgrade recruits with new skills and weapons, and even give them stylish headgear. The campaign runs roughly 15 to 20 hours, with New Game+ afterward, and it welcomes newcomers while still offering depth for veterans. The soundtrack is by Steam Powered Giraffe. It is single-player with full controller support, aimed at tactics fans who prefer skill over chance.
323190:
You govern the final city on a frozen Earth, managing its people and its infrastructure as society tries to survive. Cold, scarcity and tough moral choices push the city toward its breaking point.

Frostpunk is billed as a society survival game, and free updates have added an Endless Mode, a scenario called The Fall of Winterhome, character naming and a photo mode, with three paid expansions available. It is a single-player game from 11 bit studios, suited to city-builders who like grim decisions and the question of who their leader becomes.
323580:
Dying without glory, the Viking warrior Thora has to earn the gods' approval before she can enter Valhalla. Her trial takes her across a Norse purgatory, where she hunts for runes that awaken the jotun, giant elementals she faces armed with a two-handed axe, divine blessings and her own skill.

The game features hand-drawn animation, five jotun boss battles, nine large levels and an overarching story that explores how Thora lived and died. This Valhalla Edition adds Valhalla Mode, which pits you against tougher versions of the jotun. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to action-adventure fans who value exploration and art.
325520:
Ungh, a lovably chaotic Neanderthal, dozes off during his first night watch, and the village fire goes out. Banished for it, he must find a new flame, and you help him search the Stone Age world, from the inside of a dinosaur to volcanoes and even through time itself.

This puzzle-adventure responds to a single click or swipe, with intuitive puzzles that need only a little logic. The story is told with few words and a savagely funny streak. It is a single-player game from Daedalic Entertainment that suits casual adventure fans who like light puzzling and offbeat humor.
327220:
In this hand-drawn point-and-click adventure, Anna travels from the heights of Glass Mountain down into a dungeon, starting by freeing a talking teddy bear. Her tools are telekinesis, a talent for improvising, a shady fox and some creative misuse of torture instruments.

The tone is a grim fairy tale with a good measure of self-irony, populated by dragons, witches and trolls. The inventory has no limit and includes a slot reserved for a baby dragon. It is the debut game of author Dane Krams, from Daedalic Entertainment, and it is single-player with full controller support, suited to adventure fans who enjoy dark fairy-tale comedy.
329380:
As a clone, you flee a sinister, high-tech testing facility laid out as a Metroidvania-style overworld of five areas and 60 levels. You rescue fellow clones as you go, dodging deadly lasers, killer robots and bosses.

Death is not permanent for a clone. There are no loading screens or lives to lose, so learning from each failure is part of the design. The game asks for quick reflexes as well as planning, and it is single-player. It suits stealth-platformer fans who enjoy trial and error and exploring a connected map.
330020:
The Bergsons are a family of heroes, and you lead them against the Corruption by fighting through dungeons and caves that are generated fresh on each run. Rather than a single character, you switch between family members, each with their own abilities, in a mix of action RPG and rogue-lite design with hack-and-slash combat.

Leveling up develops both individual heroes and the family as a whole. Online and local co-op are available, including the Story mode and Family Trials, and full controller support is included. It suits players who like story-driven action RPGs with rogue-lite runs and a focus on family.
331480:
Teddy, an estranged former minister, travels through a frozen version of Hell to find his daughter Bo, who is only three and has been taken by a twisted kidnapper. Across six levels he meets bizarre creatures, uses a slingshot to clear his path, and faces a demonic rival named Mr. Pinstripe while secrets from his own past come to light.

Thomas Brush, creator of Coma and Skinny, built the game alone over five years and composed the soundtrack. Its look and mood draw on Coraline, Alice in Wonderland and The Nightmare Before Christmas, giving it a dark storybook feel. It is a single-player adventure with full controller support, suited to players who value atmosphere, music and story.
331870:
You play one of the last shapeshifters, sent on a pilgrimage across a world that has been broken into islands floating in the sky. The journey leads through ancient ruins and temples full of puzzles and mysteries, with the goal of finding what will stop reality from falling into darkness. You can shift into bird form whenever you like to fly between the islands.

The open world is built around discovery, with hidden secrets to find, and the developers put a strong emphasis on mood and visual style. The art is minimalist but vibrant. It is a single-player game with full controller support that suits players who prefer quiet exploration and atmosphere.
332250:
Penelope pilots a spaceship across the galaxy in search of Ulysses in this fast action racing game, a science-fiction take on the Odyssey. Planets can be tackled in whatever order the player prefers. Each world has its own races, unusual situations and bosses, and finishing them unlocks permanent abilities that strengthen the ship.

Weapons can be combined and used at any moment, but every ability drains energy, so power and risk go hand in hand. The controls will feel familiar to anyone who has played Micro Machines, and a second scheme exists for newcomers. The look is loud and colourful. It supports single-player and multiplayer, and suits players who enjoy arcade racing with a risk-and-reward twist.
33230:
You play Ezio Auditore, a young Florentine noble whose family is torn apart by betrayal, which sets him on a path of revenge. His journey runs through Florence, Venice and the countryside between, with rooftop climbing, stealth kills and sword fights as your main tools. Leonardo da Vinci appears as an ally who supplies inventions.

This third-person, single-player adventure is set in large historical cities rather than closed levels, so there is plenty to wander through between missions. It follows the first Assassin's Creed and keeps its modern-day frame, in which Desmond Miles relives ancestral memories through a machine. It suits players who like stealth and traversal and care more about a revenge story than constant combat.
334940:
Yoku arrives on the tropical island of Mokumana hoping for an easy life delivering parcels, only to find that the island's ancient deity is caught in a troubled slumber. He becomes the local postman, rebuilds the post office and travels about by being flipped and bumped around like a pinball, mixing pinball mechanics with platforming and exploration.

The hand-painted island is non-linear, with several questlines that can be tackled in any order you like. The tone is bright and playful, and the pinball-platformer idea gives it a distinct feel. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who enjoy colourful exploration games built around an unusual mechanic.
336420:
Set in a post-apocalyptic Sweden, this hero defense game, seen from above, has you and your friends guarding a missile silo against waves of beasts, outlaws and bosses. It is a spin-off from the world of Krater. You pick from eight gladiators with different abilities and play styles, then combine them into a crew.

Combat is quick and old school. Attacks range from gunfire and heavy blows to electricity and life-draining, and some characters can heal their allies. Scores feed into global leaderboards, so crews can compete for rankings. Toadman Interactive and Fatshark developed it. It can be played solo, but it is built for co-op, and it suits friends who want arcade-paced teamwork with some strategy.
337480:
Four undead Norse warriors, among them Gunborg and Hedgy, are sent to recover Odin's lost eye in this brawler for one to four players. The adventure runs through more than 25 levels in eight worlds, taking in a gingerbread swamp and the inside of the Midgaard Serpent, with five versus arenas on the side.

Each Viking has unique power moves, and over 40 unlockable weapons leave plenty of room to experiment. Zach Weinersmith of SMBC Comics wrote the story, and the tone is absurd and comic. Zoink Games developed it. You can play alone, or with friends online or offline, which suits groups looking for a silly co-op brawler.
339190:
Michael wakes in a dark, ruined world with no memory of who he is or what happened outside, and he has to piece it together while reality around him seems to be fading away. Dead Synchronicity is a point-and-click adventure, the first part of a series, set after a catastrophe known as the Great Wave.

The tone is bleak and unsparing, built around identity, loss and a dying universe, and the story carries a sense of urgency as time itself begins to dissolve. It is single-player and driven by puzzles and dialogue. It suits adventure fans who want a mature, grim story rather than a light one.
351920:
Each puzzle in Crazy Machines 3 gives you a goal and a set of missing parts, and your job is to place them so that a chain reaction runs from start to finish. The tasks range from punching a statue in the face to getting a worn-out space taxi running, in the Rube Goldberg tradition of overbuilt contraptions.

Physics drives everything, including forces such as wind, lightning, lasers, explosions and electricity, and chips let you give objects individual properties. The puzzles are built in 3D. Steam Workshop support allows players to make and share their own machines. It is single-player, and it suits tinkerers and puzzle fans who enjoy experimenting with cause and effect.
351970:
Two nations are at war across a medieval fantasy realm, and Sorey takes on the role of the Shepherd. His task is to stand against human darkness and the Malevolence it breeds, and to bring humans and Seraphim together again. His friend Mikleo and Lailah, keeper of the Sacred Blade, travel with him as a hidden power gathers in the background.

Tales of Zestiria is a role-playing game with a battle system built around fusions between Sorey and the Seraphim, and fights take place inside the exploration environments instead of on separate screens. Animated sequences come from the studio ufotable. It has full controller support and is listed with multiplayer, and it suits fans of anime-styled party RPGs.
356190:
Mordor is the battleground in this open-world action RPG set in Middle-earth. You build a personal army of orcs, craft a fresh Ring of Power, and lead massive assaults on fortresses to take the region from within, all while facing Sauron and his Ringwraiths.

The Nemesis System gives enemies and followers individual identities and histories, so rivalries and betrayals play out differently for each player, and past encounters shape how those characters treat you later. It is a single-player game with full controller support, and it suits players who enjoy combat-heavy adventures with strategic army-building and personal rivalries.
363600:
Running a weapon shop in a world populated by potatoes is the whole job here. You put potato smiths to work forging weapons, sell them to heroes heading out on quests, and gradually expand the business into new areas. The numbers are large for a lighthearted sim: more than 200 weapons, 70 potato heroes, 30 smiths and 20 regions, plus a potato dog you can adopt.

The design takes cues from Recettear, Game Dev Story and Weapon Shop de Omasse, so it fits players who enjoy shop management and steady growth. Pop-culture heroes make guest appearances, and the soundtrack is by Kimura Masahiko, with earlier credits on Suikoden. It is single-player.
367500:
Three AI companions called Pawns travel with you through the large open world of Dragon's Dogma: Dark Arisen. They fight on their own, using abilities shaped by what they have learned from the player. The action centres on big monsters: you can slice the heads off a hydra, climb onto griffins to fight in the air, and work out a dragon's weaknesses.

On PC, players can share their Pawns online to earn rewards and advice, and can borrow other players' Pawns when a quest calls for particular skills. Capcom developed this single-player game, which has full controller support. It suits players who like action combat against large creatures and a cooperative AI party.
368080:
Only people of the firmest belief can control Aurion, the energy that links all human wills. In Aurion: Legacy of the Kori-Odan, you play as a Kori-Odan caught in a war that has lasted 5,000 years, fighting as Enzo and calling on Erine as you uncover the secrets of the bloodline.

Combat is real-time and anime-styled, inspired by older 2D Tales games. Dash attacks leave enemies open before you use skills, and you can chain normal attacks into special and top-tier skills drawn from a pool of more than 50, in both aerial and grounded forms. The game also includes Aurionic awakenings. It is single-player with full controller support, and suits fans of action RPG combat.
368260:
You play the Hunter, a customizable original hero and demon slayer who leads a team of Marvel Super Heroes and supernatural fighters against Lilith's demonic forces and Chthon, an elder god. Between missions you build friendships with characters such as the Avengers and the X-Men, among others, and choose how your hero reacts to situations.

The game pairs RPG-style story, relationships and progression with card-based tactics, so battles are turn-based fights where you play cards for attacks and abilities. It sits in the darker corner of the Marvel Universe. Firaxis Games, known for its strategy titles, developed it. It is single-player only and suits tactics fans and Marvel followers who enjoy character-driven stories.
368340:
Retro 16-bit visuals frame this 2D action RPG, which takes place in a far-off future. Its science-fiction story unfolds through fast combat, Zelda-style puzzle dungeons, and a wide variety of equipment and skills to collect and choose from.

Battles ask you to use the tools picked up along the journey to uncover and take advantage of enemy weaknesses, while the equipment and skill choices add depth for players who want to build their character. The mix of puzzles and RPG progression is meant to balance two genres rather than favour one. CrossCode is single-player with full controller support, and it suits fans of SNES-era action RPGs who like fast-paced combat.
370910:
In the 1990s, a determined journalism student named Kathy sets out on her motorcycle to investigate the death of her grandfather, Joseph Rain, which is wrapped in mystery. Armed with a notepad and a pack of cigarettes, she works through the clues he left in Conwell Springs, a town where a local mystery and a string of people going mad point toward something dark.

Kathy Rain is a single-player point-and-click adventure, drawn in low-resolution pixel art in a 4:3 format. The story also forces her to face her troubled past. It suits fans of classic adventure games who like a mystery with a serious tone, plenty of dialogue and puzzle solving.
371520:
The American West of the 19th century is the backdrop for this strategy and simulation game about running a train. You acquire a legendary steam locomotive, fit it out with equipment until it becomes a fortress on rails, hire a crew, and earn a living by hauling goods and passengers across dangerous country.

Problems can be handled by talking, fighting or paying, and quests bring encounters with notorious bandits and other enemies. The game draws on accurate historic events and period inventions, which gives the management a grounded context. It is single-player, and it suits players who enjoy planning, resource management and a Wild West theme.
3720:
World domination is the goal in this strategy game, where you play a scheming supervillain. You pick one of three notorious masterminds as your figurehead, build a secret base from over 300 objects, from laboratories to kung fu academies and rocket caverns, and work toward a doomsday device and total control.

Running the lair means managing minions, and defending it means setting traps and devices to deal with the government agents who turn up to interfere. The tone parodies spy-film villainy with dry, dark humour. Elixir Studios developed it. It is single-player, and it suits fans of base-building management games who like their strategy with a sense of humour.
373420:
You lead a pair of Source Hunters who begin by looking into a murder in the coastal town of Cyseal, an inquiry that grows into something far larger. Fights are turn-based and the terrain matters: oil burns, water conducts electricity, and poison clouds can be ignited. Between battles you roam an open map, talk to nearly everyone, and tackle quests and puzzles in whatever order you like.

This Enhanced Edition adds voice acting, full controller support and local co-op, so two people can share one party on one screen. It is a slow, tactical, text-rich role-playing game for players who enjoy building characters and experimenting with systems, and it works well solo or with a friend.
373930:
Three campaigns put you in command of Allied, German or Soviet forces on World War II battlefields in this real-time strategy game. More than 100 units are available, including the Heinkel He 111 bomber, the T-34 tank, the Hawker Typhoon fighter and the Tiger tank.

New to the series is a choice of nine commanders, among them George Patton and Bernard Montgomery, each with unique abilities that support different styles of attack. Over 20 single-player scenarios and a skirmish mode built around challenges provide the content. Tactics include exploiting weak spots in armour, ambushing, and garrisoning buildings with infantry. The game suits strategy fans who like to plan engagements carefully.
378540:
After a catastrophe on your first day at the CREO megacorporation, you wake in a heavy-duty exoskeleton inside a wrecked part of the complex. Malfunctioning robots, deranged augmented co-workers and a rogue AI all want you dead, and you have to fight your way through them.

Combat is close-range and deliberate, and you can target specific limbs on an enemy. Whatever you cut off can drop as loot, which feeds into upgrading and crafting weapons and armour. Deck13 developed this single-player sci-fi action RPG, which has full controller support. It suits players who enjoy challenging melee fights and loot-driven progression.
379720:
A research base on Mars has been overrun by demons, and you are the lone marine sent to clear it, moving from corridors and labs down into Hell itself. Combat rewards aggression: close-range finishing moves leave health behind, chainsaw kills drop ammunition, and hiding behind cover gets you nowhere. Weapons such as the shotgun, plasma rifle and rocket launcher can be upgraded with modifications.

Id Software built this reboot around speed, so jumping, double jumping and ledge grabs matter as much as aiming, and a heavy metal soundtrack drives the pace. Multiplayer modes and SnapMap, a tool for building and sharing your own levels, extend it past the campaign. It suits players who want a fast, loud, demanding shooter.
3830:
Razputin, a young psychic, sneaks into a summer camp for psychic training in the hope of joining the Psychonauts, an elite international group of agents. He soon learns that someone is kidnapping the other campers and stealing their brains, and it falls to him to stop it.

Raz uses telekinesis, levitation and, above all, the ability to enter other people's minds, and each mind is its own level shaped by its owner. Psychonauts is a 3D action platformer from Double Fine Productions, released in 2006, with a comic and strange tone. It is single-player, and it suits players who enjoy imaginative platforming with strong humour.
383270:
The colour of the background decides which obstacles stand in your way in this puzzle-adventure. The setting begins as a dangerous grey land, and you gather coloured fragments while searching for your missing mother. Any obstacle that matches the current background colour disappears, so switching colours opens up new routes and new puzzles.

The story deals with love, loss and remorse, and a cast of talkative characters each have their own personalities. The art uses stark silhouettes with bold colours, backed by more than 30 original music tracks and voiced narration. It is a single-player game with full controller support, and it suits puzzle-platformer fans who want a reflective story.
384110:
An unstoppable, deadly plague is wiping out a strange town on the steppe, one that grew up around a huge slaughterhouse and has a peculiar social order that formed across generations. You take control of one of three characters and try to save it. Pathologic Classic HD is a restored edition of the original psychological survival game from Ice-Pick Lodge, played in first person.

Expect an unsettling, oppressive mood rather than a conventional action adventure. Prayer and science have both failed the townspeople, and the story is built around that desperation. It is a single-player game with full controller support. It suits players who want a strange, atmospheric survival experience and are willing to engage with an unusual design.
390290:
Waking from a nightmare, Bulb Boy finds that his family has vanished from the Bulbhouse and monsters are lurking in the shadows. Using the glowing glass bulb he has for a head, he sets out to defeat the creatures and rescue relatives, including Mothdog and Grandpa-raffin, from the darkness.

This is a 2D point-and-click horror adventure built around puzzles and monster encounters. It takes inspiration from Machinarium and Gobliiins, and tells a twisted tale in which Bulb Boy's abilities gradually unfold. It is a single-player game, and it suits adventure fans who like a macabre, quirky atmosphere with mouse-driven puzzle solving.
390720:
Instead of controlling a single hero, you command an entire crowd of rioters in Anarcute. Evil corporations have taken over the world's major cities, controlling the media and brainwashing the police, and your revolt takes on the Brainwash Patrol.

Waking up more people makes the crowd larger and unlocks stronger abilities, and the city, with its phone booths, fire hydrants and other props, becomes a playground for colourful destruction. Adorable visuals contrast with the large-scale chaos. It is a single-player action game with full controller support, and it suits players who like cheerful, destructive arcade action built around crowds.
391220:
Lara Croft digs into an old mystery that puts her up against a ruthless organization called Trinity. This listing is the 20 Year Celebration edition, which combines the base game with a Season Pass of extra content.

The extras include the Blood Ties story set in Croft Manor, Lara's Nightmare, in which the manor is defended against a zombie invasion, an Endurance mode for online co-op, and an Extreme Survivor difficulty. Earlier DLC adds a tomb tied to Baba Yaga and a survival challenge against infected predators. Crystal Dynamics led development. It is single-player with full controller support and VR support listed, and it suits action-adventure fans who like exploring tombs.
39190:
The hero of Dungeon Siege starts out as a simple farmer, then travels across an unbroken 3D fantasy world, gaining skills and gathering a group of as many as eight companions to meet the armies of evil spreading across the land. The world is designed to be explored seamlessly, without stops between areas.

Combat is real-time and constant, with one large battle after another as a bigger plot gradually becomes clear. Gas Powered Games developed this single-player RPG. It suits players who like classic party-based action RPGs with an emphasis on exploring and fighting.
3920:
The Caribbean is open to you in Sid Meier's Pirates!, where you can attack every ship that crosses your path or work as a privateer for a nation. Either way, the life you lead is yours to choose: raid villages, dig for buried treasure, court the daughters of governors, evade capture and face enemies who keep coming back.

The aim is to rise to fame as one of history's well-known pirates, and each choice shapes your career. Firaxis Games developed this version, released in 2005. It is single-player, and it suits players who enjoy open-ended seafaring adventure that mixes ship battles, exploration and strategy.
396750:
Space combat meets roguelike structure in this single-player shooter. You fly a ship through a changing universe, shooting enemies, crafting and looting as you try to survive against heavy odds. Every run presents new situations, and death is not the end, since it leads into a larger journey.

A story about the pilot's own existence emerges through meetings with characters who each hold a different piece of it. Rockfish Games developed EVERSPACE, and it puts weight on its visuals, with VR support listed alongside full controller support. It suits players who like roguelike repetition, improvisation and space dogfights.
397540:
Pick from four fresh Vault Hunters and travel to new worlds to stop the Calypso Twins, cult leaders who want to unite the bandit clans and seize the galaxy's greatest power. Borderlands 3 is a shooter-looter RPG, and guns are a big part of the draw, with a huge variety to find along the way.

Each Vault Hunter has distinct abilities, a deep skill tree and customization options, so the game plays differently depending on who you pick. You can play alone or team up with friends in co-op, online or over LAN. Gearbox Software developed it, and it has full controller support. It suits players who love loot, irreverent humour and shooters.
400170:
Van Helsing and his ghostly companion, Lady Katarina, explore Borgovia, a gothic-noir setting where experimental science disturbs the balance between monsters and humans. The path leads from wilderness to the dark districts of a city warped by mad science.

Van Helsing: Final Cut gathers three stand-alone episodes into one continuous story, with a campaign of more than 50 hours, six playable classes, and an endgame mode added for this edition that offers many open missions. Developed by NeocoreGames, it can be played solo or in co-op. It suits action RPG fans who enjoy loot, character builds and a gothic setting.
401680:
The POSTAL Dude is trying to survive in a town gone mad with violence, and this remake of the original isometric twin-stick shooter, now in high definition, puts you in his shoes. Armed gunmen wait around every corner, so the aim is to take them out before they take you out, using a large arsenal.

The remake refreshes the visuals, music, sound and dialogue and modernizes the gameplay. Multiplayer includes online co-op for up to four players and online deathmatch for up to eight. The tone is dark and surreal, with very violent content. Running With Scissors developed it. It suits shooter fans who like arcade twin-stick action and a deliberately provocative sense of humour.
40350:
In 1936, Fenton Paddock, a British ex-soldier turned small-time smuggler, agrees to search for Richard, a friend who vanished in Tibet. The trail carries him across several continents while German soldiers chase supernatural relics on behalf of the Nazi regime, and the two quests keep crossing paths. The setting leans on 1930s exotic locations and pulp adventure.

This is a classic point-and-click adventure built on collecting items, combining them and talking to characters to move the plot forward. Animation Arts, the studio behind the Secret Files games, developed it as a single-player experience. It appeals to players who enjoy puzzle-driven exploration, travel across varied locations and a story with an old-fashioned adventure-film tone and a hapless hero.
403640:
Choose between Empress Emily Kaldwin and her royal protector, Corvo Attano, in this first-person action game about a supernatural assassin. The world blends mysticism and industry, and each character has unique powers plus their own weapons and gadgets for dealing with enemies.

How you tackle a mission is up to you: you can stay unseen, rely on brutal combat, or mix the two. Dishonored 2 is the sequel to Arkane Studios' Dishonored and keeps the focus on player choice. It is a single-player game, and it suits players who enjoy stealth action and creative problem solving with supernatural abilities.
403940:
Each floor is a randomly built dungeon where you choose your path, fight whatever you meet, including undead cattle and oversized fungi, and look for keys that open the way deeper. Four heroes with different play styles are available to upgrade, and the content is spread over three worlds containing eighteen dungeons, bosses, merchants, side quests and a few hidden mini games.

It is the third entry in a series from the two-person Russian studio Red Winter. The tone is light and the rules are easy to learn, but the randomness and permanent risk make runs tense. Dungelot suits players who like short, replayable roguelike sessions, simple controls and steady character progression, all in single-player.
407810:
Enemies arrive in large numbers in this single-player first-person shooter, set in a cyberpunk world with highly destructible environments and a varied selection of weapons. Hard Reset Redux rebuilds the original game with reworked gameplay, upgraded visuals and extra content, while including everything from earlier editions.

The campaign is intended to be tough, and the game is built around fast, aggressive shooting. Flying Wild Hog developed it, and it supports full controller use. It suits players who enjoy old-fashioned, high-intensity shooters with a cyberpunk look and no multiplayer component, and who want a hard fight.
40800:
Rescuing a girlfriend made of bandages is the goal for a cube of meat, who must get past a tuxedo-clad fetus in a jar. Super Meat Boy sends him wall-jumping across buzz saws, crumbling caves and worlds that include hospitals, factories and hell in a punishing precision platformer.

The difficulty takes cues from NES classics such as Mega Man 2 and the Japanese Super Mario Bros. 2, starting hard and climbing to brutal. There are more than 300 levels, and the Steam version adds a playable character called Head Crab. Controls are tight and retries are instant, so it suits players who enjoy fast, twitchy platforming and can take repeated failure.
410710:
System Shock: Enhanced Edition rebuilds the original first-person immersive sim from its source code, a project handled by Nightdive Studios. The game mixes action, adventure and RPG elements, and casts you aboard the space station Citadel against the hostile AI SHODAN.

Upgrades include resolutions up to 4K, mouselook, rebindable controls, an adjustable field of view and a choice between Direct3D and OpenGL, plus an option to use either the newer Mac artwork or the old DOS artwork. Fan-made missions and mods are officially supported. It is single-player, and it suits players curious about the roots of immersive sims who are willing to accept an older design.
412020:
The year is 2036, twenty-five years after nuclear war, and Artyom must leave the wrecked Moscow Metro behind. Metro Exodus is a first-person shooter that sends him by train across the Russian wilderness after the apocalypse, with a story that spans a full year.

Levels are larger and less linear than before, with survival elements and room for sandbox-style exploration. Resources are scarce and the world is hostile, so careful play matters. Owners of the game are also entitled to an enhanced PC version with upgraded visuals. 4A Games developed it. It is single-player with full controller support, and suits players who like story-led shooters with survival pressure.
418240:
Edo-period Japan is the setting for this tactical stealth game, in which a new Shogun imposes peace across the country and recruits five specialists in assassination, sabotage and espionage. You command the team as it slips into castles, mountain monasteries and forest hideouts, choosing how to get past dozens of enemies.

Each operative has distinct skills, from Hayato, a nimble ninja with a sword and shuriken, to the samurai Mugen, and they build trust and personal stories over the missions. You can set traps, poison enemies or avoid contact entirely. Mimimi Games developed it, with full controller support. It is single-player and suits players who enjoy planning and patient real-time tactics.
421050:
Rufus wakes from a nightmare in which he saves Deponia by sacrificing himself and ends up with a mustache. Convinced these events must never happen, he teams up with McChronicle, an eccentric scientist who studies time anomalies, and discovers that visitors from the future have left a time machine lying around near his home.

Deponia Doomsday is a comedy point-and-click adventure from Daedalic Entertainment, and a later entry in the Deponia series, where Rufus tries to change the planet's fate through time travel without destroying it. Jokes and puzzle chains drive the experience. It is single-player, and it suits adventure fans who enjoy absurd humour and inventory puzzles.
421170:
Ajna is a headstrong young woman raised by her father at the edge of a rural town, until an attack on her home awakens a mysterious power inside her. She embarks on a journey across a large fantasy world to protect everything she knows.

Along the way she meets many Incarnations, people who can join her fight, and the roster grows to dozens of playable characters. Lab Zero Games, the studio behind Skullgirls, hand-drew the art and animation for this action RPG platformer, which mixes platforming with real-time combat and draws on many cultures and mythologies. Shared or split-screen co-op is supported alongside single-player.
42120:
Teams of gunslingers clash in this third-person shooter built around team-based multiplayer in classic Western settings. Matches use game modes and levels designed for coordinated play, and players choose among four characters, each with their own strengths and weak points.

A synergy system hands out power-ups that reward players for cooperating, which pushes teams toward tactics rather than lone heroics. The game mixes frantic gunfights with objective-focused play. Fatshark developed Lead and Gold, and Steam lists it as multiplayer only. It suits groups who want an online team shooter with a Wild West theme.
421740:
You play Abigail Blackwood, a young woman who has risen from the grave as a ghost, in this point-and-click adventure. Forty years have passed since her family's mad experiments, and she knows nothing of what followed. Exploring the ruined village of Oakmarsh near Coventry and the remains of Blackwood Manor, she pieces together how the household came to fall.

The game is a 2D Victorian mystery spread across more than 90 rooms in five distinct areas. Its mood is gothic and story-led, built around exploration and puzzle solving rather than action. It is a single-player experience that suits fans of classic point-and-click adventures who like a ghostly, atmospheric setting.
435100:
Mr. Smith is a former detective whose wife was killed and whose children were taken. In the city of Gloomywood, where a run of kidnappings has left residents terrified, he sneaks into the hideouts of deranged killers, searches for clues about their crimes and leads captive children out to safety.

Designer Frédérick Raynal, who also created Alone in the Dark, built this bleak stealth game around caution and cunning. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who want a grim, tense adventure about patience, risk and rescue.
436000:
Across more than a hundred levels in four worlds, this first-person game asks you to shoot and jump your way through puzzles built from moving targets and incoming projectiles. Clearing a stage means timing shots, jumps and dodges precisely. Unlockable modifiers let you replay levels in Mirror and Fast versions, and collectible evidence points to a mystery behind the arcade.

Dying and retrying quickly is part of the rhythm, so it suits players who enjoy precision challenges and learning a stage by repetition. The look is bright and cheerful, the soundtrack is by Calum Bowen, and it is single-player with full controller support.
437630:
Berlin, 2048: resources are scarce, the air and water are polluted, and drones and humanoid robots fill public jobs while surveillance is everywhere. Richard Nolan, a journalist who speaks out against this trend, wakes in a hospital after an explosion to find his wife and son missing. His search draws him into a conflict between a grim physical world and the promise of a digital paradise.

This futuristic thriller from Daedalic Entertainment explores transhumanism and themes of separation and reunification. It is a single-player, story-driven adventure with full controller support, suited to players who enjoy serious science fiction and character drama over action.
446840:
With a paint cannon in hand, a young hero takes on Le Docteur, the greedy owner of the Inkorp factory, to free the workers known as Splashers. Each color of paint does something different, letting you stick to walls and ceilings, bounce to high ledges or fool enemies, so movement depends on picking the right color for each obstacle.

The levels are packed with traps and security machinery that call for agility, quick reflexes and a willingness to learn from failed attempts. A cartoon setting and a humorous tone keep things light. It is a single-player 2D platformer with full controller support, suited to players who like fast, demanding action.
447120:
You roam a 3D map of the United States during the Great Depression, in a version of the country steeped in folklore. Along the way you meet strangers, listen to their stories and collect tales that can be retold to other people to open up new conversations. Matching the right story to a character's needs is how you move forward, so stories serve as a kind of currency.

Hand-drawn 2D illustrations accompany each encounter and give the game a storybook look. It is an unhurried, reflective single-player narrative adventure about travel, storytelling and survival, with full controller support. It suits players who prefer reading, conversation and quiet exploration to combat or time pressure.
454410:
Earth has been overrun by robot invaders, and Reika Rekkeiji, a young girl given cybernetic powers after nearly dying, is humanity's best hope against the Ajeet. In this Game Freak action platformer, she smashes enemies and chunks of the environment, then gathers the debris and shapes it into weapons and tools that clear obstacles, solve puzzles and push back against the invaders.

Platforming, combat and physics-based puzzles are blended throughout, so every stage asks what can be broken and what can be built from the wreckage. It is a single-player game suited to players who enjoy inventive action and experimenting with how objects behave.
456670:
Every quest begins as a card in this adventure, where a mysterious figure called the Dealer lays out encounters on a table. You choose which cards go into the deck, then move a token through the events, choices and dangers that turn up. When an encounter ends in a fight, the game switches to real-time combat.

The sequel adds companion characters who can fight beside you and offers 22 new challenges that test your deck-building. Single-player with full controller support, it suits players who like dark fantasy, replayable runs and a blend of tabletop-style decisions with action.
45760:
This expanded edition of Capcom's one-on-one fighting game adds five fighters and six stages, tweaks the balance of the gameplay and introduces some original modes. The costumes released earlier as downloadable content for the previous edition are also included. Fights are duels where timing, spacing and special moves decide the outcome.

You can play alone or against other people in player-versus-player matches, and the game supports controllers fully. It suits fighting game fans who enjoy learning character matchups, practicing combos and competing, as well as returning players who want a larger roster to explore.
458770:
Rally racing here means running timed stages one car at a time against the clock on gravel, tarmac and snow, with a co-driver reading pace notes while weather, night sections and mechanical failures keep changing the job. It covers the official 2016 season, including Rally China and the Super Special Stages, with the licensed cars and drivers.

Beyond the career, you can take on weekly online challenges and global leaderboards, or share a screen for local split-screen races. Full controller support makes it comfortable on a gamepad. It fits players who enjoy simulation-leaning driving, learning tracks and trimming seconds, and it is about precision and survival more than wheel-to-wheel racing.
461950:
Jack Kelly used to be a detective, but he has been framed for murder and now walks a beat in Brooklyn. Each shift mixes everyday police work, such as writing tickets and scolding pedestrians, with the bigger job of finding out who set him up, while a hostile boss, the local mafia and trouble at home all push back.

Pixel art and a 1980s cop-show style set a gritty, darkly funny tone. The story is nonlinear with multiple endings, so choices on the street matter. It is a single-player game for those who enjoy crime stories, black humor and a mix of detective work with routine patrol duty.
46500:
Kate Walker is a New York lawyer sent to an alpine valley to close a deal on a factory that builds automatons. The errand turns into a long search for Hans, the inventor linked to the factory, taking her across Europe and toward the remote east of Russia. Along the way she meets unusual characters and visits strange places, and the trip makes her question her own life.

This is a single-player adventure driven by story, conversation and puzzles, set among automatons and mechanical curiosities. The pace is unhurried, so it suits players who enjoy exploration, atmosphere and a travelogue-style plot.
46510:
The factory deal is done, yet Kate Walker's journey is far from over. Instead of going home, she joins the elderly, eccentric Hans Voralberg on his long-running quest to track down the last surviving mammoths of legend, in a forgotten land called Syberia.
