Dangers along the way test the pair far more than anything before.

Like the first game, it is a single-player adventure built around exploration, dialogue and puzzle solving. Playing the original first makes the story easier to follow, and the sequel suits those who enjoy deliberate, story-led adventures with a surreal, storybook quality.
465200:
Ink is a precious resource and each room works as a panel in this fast roguelike run-and-gun, staged inside a living comic book. You play a hero created by John Kowalsky, an author in a creative slump, and each run through the changing pages reveals more about why he has lost faith in his own creation. Your arsenal grows and your hero improves from run to run.

Killing quickly builds a fury state that lets you rip through enemies without taking damage. You can play solo, with a friend on the same screen, or online. The developers cite Rogue Legacy, Dead Cells, Contra and Metal Slug as influences, so it suits fans of run-and-gun action and roguelites.
465280:
John Yesterday and his partner Pauline are immortal, but each time John dies and returns he forgets who he is. The story runs in two timelines: present-day Paris, where the couple search for an artifact needed to remake the potion behind their condition, and flashbacks to 1481, when a young John is suspected of witchcraft and imprisoned by the Inquisition. Old acquaintances have their own plans for him.

Made by Pendulo Studios, which also made Runaway, it is a single-player adventure that moves between eras and across the world. It supports controllers fully and suits players who like mystery, conspiracy and puzzle-driven storytelling.
473690:
Waking as a Prospect in the broken lands of the former Adal Empire, you wear a mask that protects you against hunger, thirst and death. The Guides who now rule the land are testing whether you deserve a place among the Absolvers, so you travel the ruined territory, meet other Prospects, pick up weapons and armor, and learn new fighting styles before joining others in arena combat.

Combat is real-time and built around four stances, with a customizable set of moves. Online play covers both PvP and co-op, and a single-player route is available too. It suits players who enjoy melee fighting systems they can study and tailor, within a mysterious setting.
475550:
You run an apartment block on behalf of a totalitarian state, and your real job is to watch the people who live there. While tenants are out, you plant listening devices and search their belongings for anything threatening to the authorities, then build profiles and decide whether to report them. Running the building day to day continues alongside the spying.

In this dystopian setting, every report is a moral decision, and your choices shape what happens to the tenants. It is a single-player blend of adventure, strategy and management, suited to players who enjoy tense, narrative-driven games about ethics under pressure rather than fast action.
48000:
A boy enters a dark, monochrome world in search of his sister. This is a 2D puzzle platformer in which you guide him from left to right through forests, industrial settings and other hazards, working out how to get past traps and obstacles. There is no spoken dialogue, so you learn by watching, experimenting and, often, dying and trying again.

Developed by Playdead, it relies on black-and-white visuals and a quiet, unsettling mood to tell its story. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who like atmospheric puzzle platforming and are content to figure things out without instructions.
48190:
Ezio, a Master Assassin, takes his fight against the Templar Order to Rome, a city defined by power, greed and corruption, continuing the story from the earlier Ezio games. Beyond sneaking and striking, he must build up and direct a Brotherhood of fellow assassins, calling on them for help during missions.

This entry also introduces the series' first multiplayer mode, in which you choose from a range of characters with their own weapons and assassination methods and play against others online. It combines single-player and multiplayer, and suits fans of historical action adventure, especially those who have played the earlier games.
489630:
Once a peaceful world of interest to archaeologists, Gladius Prime changes when ancient relics unearthed by colonists awaken something terrible. This 4X strategy title is played in turns: you lead one of four Warhammer 40,000 factions, Orks, Necrons, Space Marines or the Astra Militarum, as they explore, expand, research and fight over the planet's resources. Each faction has its own playstyle.

Opponents can be AI or human, and the game supports co-op over the internet, a local network or split screen, alongside competitive online play. A single-player mode is available too. It suits strategy fans who like the 4X structure and want a Warhammer 40,000 setting.
492180:
Life as a scribe is quiet in a medieval town crowded with warriors, sorcerers and dragons, until one book changes everything for the young Haimrik. Accompanied by Masamba, a lioness who guards him while eyeing him as a meal, he goes after an evil king and the generals known as the Word Warriors. The words under his feet come alive as he steps on them, and choosing the right ones lets him defeat enemies and solve puzzles.

The game turns language into a mechanic, with crisp humor and an unusual visual style. It is a single-player action adventure with full controller support, suited to players who like word-based puzzles mixed with light action.
493340:
Roller coasters are the centerpiece of this theme park builder. You lay paths, place scenery, customize rides and assemble attractions piece by piece from more than a thousand building components, while also shaping the land into hills, lakes and caves. Coasters can be routed above ground and below it, so layout is as much a design choice as a technical one.

Creative freedom is the main draw: you can recreate real rides or invent your own, and the park works as a living world. It is single-player and suits builders who enjoy designing and decorating at least as much as managing finances.
493540:
Inside a human mind, a surreal place built from thoughts, memories and inner voices, nightmarish creatures have started to spread fear after years of calm. You guide Dusty, the mind's grumpy former voice of courage, and his upbeat friend Piper through its different regions, solving puzzles, fighting off nightmares and trying to bring back the lost courage.

Music is central to this action-adventure, and humor lightens a story about facing fears. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who enjoy imaginative, colorful worlds and a mix of light puzzles and combat.
493900:
The Dungeon Lord has brought the evil factions together and now wants to expand his dark empire. You dig out an underground lair and fill it with rooms, traps and structures, then recruit monsters such as orcs, succubi and zombies. When the army is ready, you lead it up into the overworld to take on the do-gooders, with Thalya, a dark elf priestess, serving as your lieutenant at the front.

The game presents dungeon management and army-led conquest from a villain's point of view, with a humorous tone. Besides the single-player campaign, it offers multiplayer and online co-op, and it supports controllers fully. It suits strategy and simulation fans who enjoy playing the bad guy.
49520:
Shooting and looting drive this first-person role-playing game, which offers an enormous supply of guns to find. You pick from four vault hunters, the Siren, Commando, Gunzerker or Assassin, and fight across a living planet full of creatures and psychos, chasing revenge against the villain Handsome Jack. Each class has its own skills, and the Gunzerker can wield two guns at once.

The game can be played alone or in four-player co-op, and it has full controller support. It has a comedic, irreverent tone and a loot-driven cycle of fighting, collecting and upgrading. It suits players who enjoy shoot-and-loot games and want to team up with friends.
501300:
As Edith Finch, you return to the sprawling family house in Washington state to find out why you are the last of the Finches still alive. Each story you uncover lets you live through a relative's final day from a first-person view, with the tales spanning generations, from long ago to modern times. Together they form a collection of strange family tales.

Because every story has its own mechanics and mood, the game keeps changing form as you move through the house. It is a single-player narrative adventure with full controller support, suited to players who prefer story, atmosphere and exploration to combat or challenge.
503560:
Emergency calls come in, and as the dispatcher you decide what happens next. Depending on the situation, you might talk someone through first aid, offer advice, send the right number of police, fire or ambulance units, or conclude that a call is a prank and ignore it. Callers range from desperate relatives to people just wasting your time.

Free Play lets you pick a city anywhere in the world, using its real streets, addresses and emergency infrastructure, so you can run the dispatch center for your own hometown. It is a single-player management game about triage and time pressure, suited to players who like simulation and strategy built around judgment calls.
503940:
Starting in 1830, you head a railroad company in North America as industry booms and rivals race to build the dominant rail network. You lay track, buy trains from a catalog of more than 40 detailed models, construct stations, factories, maintenance facilities and tourist sites, and hire staff to keep services efficient. Over 300 technologies can be researched to improve both the trains and the way the company operates.

Competitors pursue the same goals, so the game combines logistics, finance and long-term planning rather than simple track-laying. It is single-player with controller support, and it suits players who enjoy building transport networks and tuning them for profit across a long span of history.
505730:
Sisters Cassie and Fay travel through a universe populated by anthropomorphic vegetables, looking for their grandfather Jiji, in this space adventure with a silly sense of humor. You manage your own spaceship, visit dozens of planets and follow a story that changes as you go, meeting a cast of lovable characters, some of them familiar faces.

Battles are tactical and turn-based, and you craft weapons from a huge selection, each with its own quirky effect. It is a single-player game with a light, goofy tone, suited to players who enjoy offbeat strategy-adventures that mix ship management, exploration and crafting.
507490:
This RTS is built around scale: huge numbers of units can be active at once as you run an army across maps big enough to cover entire worlds. Two factions, humanity's Post-Human Coalition and the Substrate, fight for the galaxy, and the story pits humanity against the new threat while rebel humans stake out their own territory.

Single-player campaigns cover several worlds, and skirmishes can be played online against opponents or alongside allies. The engine was designed for modern multi-core processors, and the game became a common benchmark for DirectX 12 performance. It is best for strategy players who like large-scale macro management over commanding a handful of heroes.
520670:
Dodgeball goes medieval here, with warriors hurling weapons at each other across a rift. You pick one of eight strikers, each with its own abilities, stats and weapon, and fight in one of four arenas whose layouts, obstacles and hazards change the tactics. Accuracy, anticipating your opponent's throws and good timing decide matches.

The game is built for local multiplayer, with split-screen play for both head-to-head and cooperative matches, and a ladder to climb. It suits groups sharing a couch and players who enjoy learning the differences between characters and outwitting a human opponent.
530390:
Skullface, a blocky slasher with a skull for a face, slides across isometric puzzle levels to dispatch camp counselors. Each stage is a logic puzzle: he moves in straight lines until something stops him, so you plan a route that reaches every victim while avoiding hazards. There are hundreds of levels, grouped into videotape-style collections.

Voxel graphics and a darkly comic tone parody 1980s slasher movies, and the kills are bloody in a cartoonish way. It is a single-player game for puzzle fans who enjoy horror comedy and do not mind gore played for laughs.
534370:
Locations in Europe, Asia and the Americas make this a farming simulator with a global reach. Each region has its own crops, including hemp, coffee and olives, and the work covers fieldwork, orchards, greenhouses, animal husbandry and green energy. You drive licensed machinery from makers such as Zetor, Landini and McCormick, modeled with attention to weight and physics.

Three game modes aim at both simulation veterans and people new to the genre, so different levels of experience are covered. It is a single-player game with controller support, suited to patient players who enjoy realistic machinery and varied agricultural work.
537800:
Before every mission, you recruit and train a crew for a World War II heavy bomber, with generated names, skills and backstories, and customize the aircraft with nose art and liveries. In flight, you direct the crew as they handle fuel, ammunition, hydraulics and repairs while enemy fighters, flak, weather and thin oxygen threaten the plane.

Death is permanent, so losing a familiar crew member carries weight. Missions are high-risk and play out in real time, with you managing the aircraft from a cutaway view. It is single-player with controller support, and it suits strategy and simulation players who like becoming attached to characters and managing crises.
539340:
No tutorial tells you what to do in this exploration-driven adventure. You uncover mysteries and solve puzzles hidden in forests, caves and other landscapes, learning through experimentation and curiosity. Wild animals live in the world: some are friendly or helpful, while others are deadly and must be avoided or turned into allies.

A detailed automap fills in as you travel, which helps when you stray from the main path. You can wander freely, hunt for secrets and get lost without being stuck for good. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who prefer discovery to instruction.
541310:
Young Thor gets the hammer Mjolnir as a birthday gift and sets off through the Northern Realms to become a god, facing mythical creatures along the way. The hammer is the core tool: you aim it freely, and it ricochets off walls and foes, allowing trick shots that clear obstacles and enemies.

The pixel art is by Henk Nieborg and the music by Chris Hülsbeck, which gives the game an authentic retro feel. It is a challenging single-player platformer with tight controls and full controller support, suited to fans of old-school 16-bit action who enjoy fast pacing.
542050:
In the Forgotten Lands, where lost and discarded things end up, creatures called Forgotlings are made from everyday objects such as old toys and letters. You play Anne, an enforcer responsible for order there, who is trying to put down a rebellion so that she and her master Bonku can return to the human world.

The hand-animated visuals give it the feel of an animated film, and the gameplay combines light puzzle platforming with a cinematic, story-focused structure, using magical abilities to affect the world. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to players who value story and art over difficulty.
544750:
Two new systems, Reversal Edge and Soul Charge, shape this weapons-based 3D fighting game. Reversal Edge lets you block an opponent's attack and counter, while Soul Charge is a temporary power-up that unlocks extra attacks. Lethal Hits add heavy combo damage. The story mode, Soul Chronicle, revisits events from the first SOULCALIBUR in the 16th century.

Other modes include online matches against players around the world and a character creation mode. It can be played alone or against others, and it suits fans of weapon-based fighters who enjoy learning a roster and mixing offense with defense.
552500:
Up to four players fight side by side against swarming enemies in this first-person melee game, which is set among the Warhammer Fantasy Battles universe. The heroes face an alliance of a Chaos army and the Skaven horde. You choose from five characters, each with three branching careers to master, and work through missions while climbing difficulty tiers that start at Recruit.

Combat is bloody, close-quarters melee, and teamwork matters because the party survives or falls together. It can be played solo or with up to three friends online. It suits fans of intense co-op action against hordes who like building a character through RPG-style progression.
558420:
Four short experimental adventures are packaged together as a compilation tape, with a remaster of its opening chapter, The House Abandon, among them. The games mix text-adventure and point-and-click styles with other approaches, building psychological horror around 1980s technology and nostalgia.

Each story changes the way you interact with it, so the game keeps shifting rather than following a single formula. Because the episodes are short, the collection can be taken in over a few sittings. It is a single-player anthology that suits players who like unusual interactive storytelling and tense, unsettling atmosphere.
559100:
In 1983, at a tense point of the Cold War, you lead the Cabal, a secret organization trying to stop a conspiracy that aims to turn world leaders and nations against each other. Between missions you investigate classified files, interrogate captured agents and manage your operatives, while the field operations themselves play out as turn-based tactics.

The tone borrows from classic spy films, with paranoia and counterintelligence at the center. The campaign runs more than 40 hours, and there is PvP multiplayer as well. It suits fans of tactical strategy who enjoy a slow-burning espionage plot.
571310:
When mysterious earthquakes strike a former trading town, a lone steambot and an unlikely companion go underground to find the cause. You dig through the earth, collecting treasure, uncovering secrets and avoiding traps while fighting a range of creatures, then use what you find to upgrade your gear so you can reach deeper areas.

Tools such as the Hookshot, for swinging over chasms, and the Jet Engine, for flying through caves, open up new routes. The design draws on Metroidvania games. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to players who like exploration, collecting and gradual upgrades.
573120:
Exiled to an unknown island, Eirik and his Viking family must survive on their own. You gather resources, secure food, ration water, organize the camp and look after each character's physical and mental well-being, including illness, injuries and bad weather. Exploring brings contact with other people, some helpful and others hostile, as well as esoteric mysteries.

RPG and adventure elements shape the management, so each character's condition and personality matter, not just the supply count. It is a single-player game that suits players who like survival management and tough decisions, with more planning than action.
578330:
Chase McCain is a police officer sent undercover to hunt down Rex Fury, a criminal who has escaped custody and caused a wave of crime across the city. The action takes place across an open world with over 20 districts to explore, vehicles to drive, car thieves to arrest and hundreds of collectibles to find.

Two players can team up in co-op. The humor is typical of LEGO games, with references to movies, and the family-friendly tone suits players of all ages. It supports full controller use and also works as a single-player game.
582160:
Ancient Egypt is the setting for this action-adventure, with deserts, oases, the Nile, the Mediterranean coast and the tombs of Giza all part of a large open world. You play Bayek, whose story leads to the beginnings of the Assassin's Brotherhood, and you take on quests, hostile factions and wild animals along the way.

Combat moves toward RPG design, with looted weapons of different rarity and characteristics, a deeper progression system and powerful bosses. It is a single-player game that suits fans of open-world action RPGs who are interested in historical settings.
585450:
This installment of the Heretic Kingdoms saga begins after the members of a secret council, the Penta Nera, are murdered and their souls consumed by demons called Devourers. The Penta Nera return as demonic versions of themselves, still pursuing power and immortality.

It is a single-player role-playing game viewed from an isometric angle, with tactical combat that unfolds in real time. The story is dark fantasy, the fights are meant to be demanding, and full controller support is included. It suits fans of isometric role-playing games who like to manage battles as they happen.
58570:
Hollywood gets a monstrous makeover in this comic adventure from Pendulo Studios. The creatures in horror films turn out to be real monsters, and some are now stuck making children's movies, romantic comedies and musicals. Unsurprisingly, they begin to rebel. You follow journalist Liz Allaire and Dan Murray as they get drawn into the chaos, solving puzzles across settings modeled on different film genres.

The studio behind the Runaway series built this one around jokes, movie tributes and a few mysteries. Its presentation aims for the look of an animated feature, with a full soundtrack and plenty of dialogue. It is single-player and suits adventure fans who enjoy silly puzzles and affectionate film parody.
589780:
In a cyberpunk city, the corporation Supercontinent is about to launch a system called Social Psyche Welfare that is meant to rid people of depression, anger and fear. A club bartender and a freelance hacker call it brainwashing and set out to stop it, aided by company staff who do not know they are being used and by a rogue android with a talent for empathy. Gameplay is conversation and craft: mixing drinks to draw out feelings, shaping pottery and impersonating others on the phone.

Developer Deconstructeam uses the thriller plot to ask what happiness is worth and how much of life is fated. It is a single-player narrative game for fans of dialogue-driven stories.
598550:
Bounty hunters take on the gangs that rule a future city in this side-scrolling run-and-gun shooter. You run, jump and duck behind cover as you fight through the streets, in a hard-boiled tone with a steady stream of jokes.

You can go it alone or bring a partner, either on the same couch or remotely through Steam Remote Play. A separate Arcade Mode pits you against players worldwide for leaderboard rankings. Full controller support makes it easy to pick up on a sofa, and it suits fans of old-school arcade action who like shooters that reward quick reactions.
606150:
Will keeps a shop in Rynoka, a village built near a set of ancient Gates that lead to other realms. He secretly wants to be a hero, so he takes his sword into the dungeons beyond the Gates and hauls treasure back to sell. The game splits its time between those two jobs: action combat with rogue-lite elements below ground, and shopkeeping above it.

What you find decides what you can sell and what gear you can afford. The current version adds Companions, extra mini-bosses and gear, more than 100 additional room layouts and a New Game+ option. Single-player with full controller support, it suits fans of dungeon crawling that feeds a small shop sim.
606280:
Fury, one of the Four Horsemen, returns to a ruined Earth with a single job: tracking down and defeating the Seven Deadly Sins. She fights in third-person melee with a whip and magic, and her different forms unlock new weapons, moves and ways to get around. The world is open-ended and interconnected, so you keep doubling back through earlier areas as new abilities let you reach places that were closed off.

This is the third main Darksiders game, made by Gunfire Games. It is a single-player hack-and-slash adventure with full controller support, and it suits players who like exploration, combat against large enemies and an apocalyptic fantasy setting.
609320:
Tracks left by a once-thriving civilization cross a seabed that has long since dried out, and you follow them in a strange sail-driven land vessel. The vehicle is the center of the game: you keep it running, repair and upgrade it, and use it to get past obstacles and harsh weather. Relics and abandoned buildings along the route hint at what happened to the people who came before.

FAR: Lone Sails is quiet and atmospheric, with drifting clouds, wind in the sails and a post-apocalypse that has no zombies, only you and your machine. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who like contemplative journeys with a hands-on, mechanical side.
612880:
B.J. Blazkowicz is back in a 1961 where the Nazis hold the world, and the United States is no exception. He fights as a Resistance member, crossing American landmarks under occupation to recruit the bravest resistance leaders left. Gameplay is a first-person shooter with a big arsenal and a set of new abilities for cutting down Nazi troops, running on id Tech 6.

MachineGames developed this sequel to Wolfenstein: The New Order, and it is a single-player campaign with no multiplayer modes. It suits players who want a story-driven shooter with a bold alternate-history premise and plenty of firepower.
617290:
Something ancient and malevolent has crossed over from another dimension and filled the world with monstrous creatures. The few humans left can open gateways to other realms, and you play a survivor who steps through them to scavenge supplies, uncover where the threat came from and fight back toward a safer foothold. It is a third-person shooter with RPG progression.

Gunfire Games built it for solo play or online co-op with up to two others. Hordes and large bosses keep the combat busy, and the worlds you visit differ between playthroughs. It suits players who like tough, loot-driven shooters and prefer to tackle them with a small team of friends.
618970:
Cutter Slade, an experienced elite soldier, lands on Adelpha, an alien planet where magic and advanced science exist side by side. The world is open to explore in any order, with cities to visit and hundreds of quests on offer from the start. The native Talans can be taken on in direct combat or avoided through stealth, and your arsenal and gadgets improve as you go.

Outcast - Second Contact is a remake of an older cult favorite that helped shape open-world adventure games. It is single-player, and it suits players who enjoy exploring at their own pace and are curious to see a classic reworked with modern visuals.
626660:
Penny dies in mysterious circumstances and wakes up as a temp covering for Death himself. The job lets her flip between the living realm and the realm of the dead, which is the core of this puzzle platformer. You jump across platforms, help restless spirits move on and possess living people, moving their limbs and reading their thoughts to solve puzzles, all while Penny works out how she died.

Zoink Games made it as a comedy, with writing by Ryan North. Single-player with full controller support, it suits players who like jokes, platforming and puzzle logic built around possession.
628800:
Bio-mechanical Meroptians bent on conquest have invaded the Omios star, and you fly the Delta Lance against them in a horizontal shoot 'em up. The game offers 21 levels split into 35 sublevels with a choice of route, plus weapons and power-ups to pick in each mission. Expect over 100 enemies, 35 bosses and hazards beyond bullets.

The design draws on classic shmups, with retro-styled art, an optional CRT monitor effect and a soundtrack of more than 60 tracks. You can play solo or in shared-screen co-op, and there is a Robot Chase spin-off. It suits genre fans who want a hard game with secrets, multiple endings and rankings.
6310:
April Ryan moves between two parallel worlds in this classic graphical adventure, one shaped by science and one by magic. You guide her through the story by exploring locations, solving puzzles, talking with the people she meets and dealing with the monsters that turn up along the way. The game is built on a large scale, with more than 150 locations across the two worlds and over 70 speaking characters.

Its developers cite more than 40 hours of play and over twenty minutes of pre-rendered cutscene video, backed by a cinematic score. Single-player and dialogue-heavy, it suits patient adventure fans who like long stories, classic puzzle structure and a strong sense of place.
631570:
Nearly a century after superintelligent AI was outlawed, Vera, a cybernetically enhanced special agent with the Central Bureau, is sent to investigate a string of brutal murders. The trail leads to fanatics determined to build exactly that kind of machine mind, while a loss from her own past returns to shake her confidence in her sanity. Her tool is Blue, a rare nano-substance that gives her abilities shaped by her mindset.

Clifftop Games and Faravid Interactive mix detective work with science fiction in a Nordic noir atmosphere. You choose how Vera uses her augmentations to investigate and gather information. It is single-player and suits narrative adventure fans who like moody crime stories.
632470:
You are a detective working a murder in a run-down city district, and almost everything about how you do it is up to you. Instead of fighting, you rely on conversation and a skill system in which your abilities speak up inside your head, arguing and pushing you toward different readings of a situation. You can question memorable characters, solve the case, accept bribes, or fall apart as a person.

The Final Cut edition adds full English voice acting, new political vision quests, an extra area and more citizens to meet. Text-heavy and strictly single-player, it suits players who want a role-playing game driven by writing and choice rather than combat.
638000:
Your task is to build the machinery that carries every passenger where they need to go. Across more than 100 levels, you put together chairlifts, gondolas, bridges and several kinds of ramp from a limited supply of materials, starting in gentle foothills and ending on exposed peaks. Rope tension and other forces behave realistically, and you also steer the passengers across the terrain, so how they fare is up to you.

Saving money by cutting corners makes construction cheaper but puts riders at risk, often with comic results. Single-player and darkly funny, it suits fans of physics puzzles and construction games who enjoy slapstick disasters.
63910:
Crossworlds packs the complete Armored Princess campaign, with its orc-themed expansion, plus two shorter modes in one standalone release. In the main campaign you guide a hero across a fantasy overworld, recruiting creature stacks and taking quests, then fight turn-based battles on a grid where each unit type has its own strengths, backed by hero spells. One mini-campaign is a run of arena boss fights; the other uses tactical scenarios with random armies on both sides.

A world editor lets you build your own maps and campaigns, and equipment sets encourage varied army builds. It is a single-player, turn-based game with a fairy-tale tone and humorous writing, suited to fans of Heroes of Might and Magic style tactics.
644830:
After a storm brings down your plane near Jericho City, you come to weeks later inside a rundown detention center. The city has fallen into chaos: armored soldiers impose martial law, robots run wild and a dark nanostorm spreads above the skyline. Combat is close-range and unforgiving, and you target and cut off enemy limbs to take their equipment and strengthen your character.

Deck13 supplies weapons, armor, abilities, implants and drones for customizing your fighter, and the setting is larger and more varied than before. Single-player with full controller support, The Surge 2 suits fans of demanding melee action RPGs who like turning each victory into new gear.
673880:
You command Tech-Priests of the Adeptus Mechanicus under Magos Dominus Faustinius on Silva Tenebris, a planet only recently found again, where the Necrons are beginning to awaken. Over 50 hand-crafted missions you manage resources, recover long-lost technology and send squads into turn-based tactical battles, where every decision carries weight.

Upgrades for your Tech-Priests include servo-skulls, support gear and other mechanical enhancements, and you pick from several character classes. Cognition points gate the strongest weapons and abilities. A single-player game from Bulwark Studios with full controller support, it suits strategy fans and Warhammer 40,000 followers who want a tactical campaign with a distinctive tech-cult flavor.
678950:
Fights in DRAGON BALL FighterZ are built around teams of three. Developed with Arc System Works, it is an anime-styled fighting game in which you pick three fighters from the Dragon Ball roster, tag them in and out, and use support moves to chain high-speed combos. Unreal Engine visuals give the battles a polished, animated look.

Online options include ranked matches, an interactive lobby and a six-player Party Match. A story mode features Android 21, a character created for the game. With both single-player and multiplayer modes and full controller support, it suits Dragon Ball fans and anyone who wants fast, flashy matches that reward practice.
682990:
You begin in a cramped, dirty hideout selling on the street and work your way up through a criminal business. Growth comes from taking over territory, recruiting minions, running labs and training staff, while you smuggle in goods from outside cartels and try not to attract the police. Nothing in the underworld is easy, and the risks climb along with the profits.

Developer Byterunners added seven free updates after release, bringing new locations, effects, mechanics and characters. This is a single-player simulation with a mature subject and a business-ladder structure, and it suits players who enjoy climbing from nothing in a dark setting. A co-op sequel exists separately.
683320:
Grief drives the journey of Gris, a young girl adrift in a faded world after something painful in her past. Her sorrow shows in her dress, which gains new powers as she moves forward, and each ability opens paths that were closed before. As the story unfolds, she changes emotionally and the world around her looks different.

There is no death, no danger and no frustration here. Light puzzles and platforming sections appear as more of the world opens up, along with optional skill-based challenges. The story comes through delicate artwork, animation and an original score, with very little text. It is single-player with full controller support, and suits anyone after a calm, visual experience.
6860:
Someone is picking off assassins from Agent 47's own agency, the ICA, which suggests a larger and more powerful organization has joined the game. Sensing he could be next, 47 heads for America and takes contracts as a professional killer. You approach each hit in third person, choosing how to reach and remove your target.

The game is organized around quiet work: quieter, more precise kills earn more money, which you can spend on paying off witnesses and police to lower the heat, buying specialist equipment and information, and modifying weapons for noise, recoil, firing speed and accuracy. Single-player Hitman suits stealth fans who enjoy planning an approach.
694280:
The resistance has beaten Zombie Hitler and banished him to Hell, yet the dead return, hungrier than ever. This third-person shooter from Rebellion, the studio behind Sniper Elite 4, continues an alternate-history story in 1940s Europe, following the Survivor Brigade through Italy and farther afield. Levels range from corpse-filled canals to a zombie zoo, and they head into stranger territory as the plan behind the outbreak unfolds.

The campaign can be played alone or in online co-op for up to four players, with occult enemies, powerful weapons and shooting at the core. It suits horror-action fans who enjoy gory zombie killing with friends.
698640:
In a dystopian future, you are a stateless outcast surviving on scraps from abandoned alien ships and stations. A rumored alien wreck hidden in the Deep Sky sector could be your ticket to citizenship and a comfortable life on a habitable planet. To find it, you recruit up to three mercenaries as a squad and explore wrecks from a scavenger base, looting for gear and clues and meeting traders and other inhabitants along the way.

The game mixes turn-based strategy with RPG elements, tactical card battles and roguelike features, all in a retro-futuristic comic-book style. Single-player with full controller support, it suits players who like squad building, gear upgrades and card-driven fights.
699170:
Kyrie is an Arbiter, a servant of the Immortal Council, which exists to preserve order across a fantasy land touched by steampunk. You lead her group of Arbiters through more than 40 story encounters in a mature narrative, with demanding end-game content waiting afterward. Battles are classic turn-based tactics on grid maps with rough terrain and elevation, set on hand-drawn backdrops.

Character building stands out. Each character's main class, secondary class and passives come from a roster of 30-plus classes and 300-plus abilities, so you can shape a flexible all-rounder or a narrow specialist. Single-player, from 6 Eyes Studio, it suits tactics fans who enjoy building their party.
700160:
Most platformers treat the ground as fixed. Semblance, set in a minimalist world where nothing is hard, lets you push, squash and reshape the terrain itself. If a collectible is out of reach, you deform and raise a section of the world to get there. Across three worlds, each exploring a different consequence of a shifting planet, you push back a crystalline growth that hardens everything it touches by freeing the life essences.

Nyamakop's game has a calm, minimalist look, full controller support and a single-player focus. It suits puzzle-platformer fans who enjoy experimenting with an unusual core mechanic.
710920:
Darksiders Genesis goes back before the original game. The Council, which maintains the Balance, sends War and Strife, two of the Horsemen, to deal with Lucifer, a demon king who is empowering master demons throughout Hell to disrupt that order. You hunt those demons through isometric-view levels, fighting with hack-and-slash combat.

Strife, the fourth Horseman, appears for the first time here, and the series gets co-op for the first time, playable online or on a shared screen as well as solo. Airship Syndicate developed it with full controller support. It suits series fans curious about the backstory and anyone who likes bringing a friend along for action-adventure dungeon runs.
711660:
Chuchel is a hairy little creature obsessed with a cherry, and his rival Kekel wants it just as badly. Each scene is a self-contained puzzle or gag that you solve by interacting with the surroundings and with the odd characters nearby, and the screen is full of quirky animation.

Made by Amanita Design, the studio behind Machinarium, Botanicula and Samorost, it leans on situational comedy rather than dialogue, and some stages riff on classic video games. The soundtrack is by the band DVA. Single-player and low on pressure, it suits players who want a silly, charming puzzle adventure.
718590:
As a Templar knight, you descend into a mysterious fallen temple to find answers and test your faith. The journey spans four distinct worlds, each filled with dark enemies and treacherous bosses, and you can pick up dozens of weapons to meet them. The tale is built on religious devotion and sacrifice, with a somber tone, as each encounter pushes your courage and conviction.

Hibernian Workshop made this a single-player action RPG with full controller support. It suits fans of grim, religious-themed dark fantasy who like tough bosses and a story that keeps asking what you are willing to give up.
718650:
When a war between ancient mages broke the planet Driftland apart, a powerful spell was all that kept its pieces together. New sources of magic have since appeared, and you are a Mage Overlord who can move floating islands and link them together, building a growing empire to restore the world to its former glory.

Star Drifters' strategy simulation mixes empire building with fantasy RPG elements. You can play alone, cooperatively online, or against other players online, so it suits fans of empire-building strategy who want a flexible mix of solo and multiplayer.
721180:
Pax, a con artist and exile with unusual abilities, takes a job hauling a package its previous owners want back across an alternate version of America by tour bus, driven by a robot. The trip is split into stops, where you talk with a crew of fellow Anomals, handle missions and brawl when talk fails. Conversation is the central mechanic: what you say changes how crew members feel about you and how scenes play out.

The tone mixes road-movie humor with serious themes, and the art leans toward a stylized, comic-book look. This single-player narrative game with action sequences suits players who like dialogue choices, character relationships and a story told through a close-knit group.
751820:
Under endless rain in an alternate 1988, a nuclear cataclysm set off by Duncan, the architect of a vast tower, has left the world in ruins. You climb the procedurally generated tower floor by floor, shooting, slashing and dashing through traps, killer AI, unhinged junkies and giant Wardens, and take out the tower's deranged owner while your heart threatens to explode.

This synth-punk roguelike from SUPERSCARYSNAKES is a 2D action shooter with upgrades that help you last longer each run. You can play alone or in split-screen co-op, with full controller support. It suits fans of fast, run-based shooters with a stylish, 1980s-flavored attitude.
752590:
France, 1348: plague is spreading through the villages and the Inquisition is hunting Amicia and her kid brother Hugo. You guide the siblings through ruined countryside, avoiding soldiers and the swarms of rats that devour anything in their path, which you keep at bay with fire and light. Along the way they team up with other children and learn to rely on each other.

Asobo Studio's story-driven, third-person action-adventure is grim in tone and centered on the bond between two siblings. It is single-player with full controller support. It suits players who like cinematic, narrative-led games with stealth and survival, and who do not mind a heavy subject.
7670:
Guns are only half of the arsenal in BioShock, a first-person shooter that also gives you genetic modification. Alongside revolvers, chemical throwers and grenade launchers, you inject plasmids that grant powers: channel electricity into water to shock groups of enemies, freeze foes solid and shatter them with a wrench, set fire to targets, or unleash hornets from your arms. You also hack devices, upgrade weapons and craft special ammo, and fights can be approached in different ways.

Developed by 2K Boston and 2K Australia, it is set in the underwater city of Rapture and is entirely single-player. It suits shooter fans who like atmosphere, a story-led campaign and RPG-style character powers.
774291:
Sentient office appliances have taken over the workplace, and you fight them from an office chair in a third-person roguelite shooter. Choose a loadout, earn XP, pick power-ups and unlock upgrades for the chair itself as waves get harder, working through grunts, minibosses and major bosses. Its structure will be familiar to fans of Megabonk, though the setting is a joke-filled corporate workplace.

DoubleMoose Games draws on the shooters of the 2000s. You can play solo or with up to three friends, and a PvP arena mode lets you test strong builds against each other. Leaderboards add score chasing. It suits fans of run-based action roguelites who like silly, over-the-top premises.
7800:
It is 1959 in Punchbowl, Pennsylvania, a retro-futuristic city that thinks it has left the past behind, and Stubbs, a determined corpse, is about to disagree. As the zombie, you tear through the living, feeding on brains to replenish gruesome weapons such as gut grenades, flinging your severed hand to possess people, and converting victims into an undead horde that follows you into the next fight.

The tone is B-movie horror comedy with a retro setting. A friend can join as Grubbs through shared-screen co-op, and the game also works as a single-player romp. It suits fans of dark comedy action who enjoy chaos, especially with a second player on the couch.
780290:
Isaac Childres' board game gets a digital adaptation in this tactical RPG, where you lead a band of mercenaries in a harsh medieval dark-fantasy setting. You take jobs from anyone who pays, whether city officials or cultists, then fight through dungeons, forests and caves in turn-based battles driven by ability cards, with every choice mattering.

Flaming Fowl Studios and Saber Interactive handle the adaptation, with solo play and online co-op, plus full controller support. It suits tactics fans who like careful planning and mercenary-for-hire storytelling, and board game fans who want it without the setup.
787810:
Ancient Titans threaten Tasos, and you set out as one of several heroes sent to stop them by clearing dungeons that are reshuffled on every run. Viewed from above in pixel art, the game borrows its feel from classic Zelda titles, with sword swings, locked doors and puzzle rooms. Each death sends you back to the start with permanent upgrades, so every attempt goes further.

Up to four players can join on the same screen or online, or you can go solo. The pace is approachable and the tone bright, a good fit for friends who want a lighthearted dungeon crawl rather than a punishing one.
793460:
You work as an emergency dispatcher for the city of your choice: answer incoming calls, send out the right units and keep an eye on how weather, traffic and the changing seasons complicate each incident. As the situation worsens, you handle natural disasters, riots, terrorist attacks and organized crime, scaling from one neighborhood up to coordinating multiple operators in major cities.

The sequel to 911 Operator offers more than 100,000 areas, including thousands of real-world cities, and shows your units at work in 3D. Jutsu Games made it for single-player use. It suits fans of management and dispatch simulation who like juggling priorities under pressure.
794540:
Lina is the only human cab driver left in Los Ojos, a city of automated vehicles, and her first night on the job goes badly when her best friend vanishes. Needing money, a place to sleep and answers, she follows the only leads she has: the passengers she picks up, from anarchist punks to corporate types to police who keep bothering her. You talk with them, deciding how open or guarded to be.

It is a narrative game, labelled a visual novel, centered on staying emotionally intact. You balance honesty and empathy against Lina's own wellbeing, and the story takes aim at late-stage capitalism. Chance Agency made it single-player, for story-first players.
798490:
The Daughters, each an echo of the greatest warrior who ever lived, are the last defense against Suffering, a force made of humanity's worst crimes. You lead them as an army in turn-based tactical battles governed by a Dynamic Timeline System, where actions and counters can be chained into elaborate sequences, and where bosses drawn from Suffering itself bring the toughest fights.

Losses are part of the design. Between battles you can sacrifice one Daughter to heal another, and survivors become stronger for the next fight. Lightbulb Crew's dark, gothic game is single-player with full controller support, and it suits tactics fans who can accept failing and rebuilding.
8000:
Lara Croft's debut adventure is rebuilt here for a newer era. She chases the legendary Scion artifact around the globe, exploring Atlantis and the pyramids of Egypt, climbing and jumping through large environments, solving puzzles and fighting enemies along the way.

Crystal Dynamics built it on an enhanced version of the Tomb Raider: Legend engine, giving Lara more fluid movement, bigger spaces, a refreshed pace and a clarified story. Single-player with full controller support, it suits series fans who want to see where it started, and players who like third-person platforming and exploration.
807120:
Here you play the villain. Iratus is a necromancer freed after a millennia-long imprisonment, and he wants to return to the surface and spread death through the mortal realms. He commands an undead army of skeletons, zombies, banshees and other creatures, stitched together from parts of enemies he has defeated. Between expeditions through twisted catacombs, you expand your underground lair and research secret rituals to strengthen your servants.

Unfrozen's game combines turn-based tactical battles with roguelike structure and RPG progression. Opponents include miners, dwarves and mercenaries who stand in your way. It is single-player and suits tactics fans who like an unusual premise and squad building.
808090:
This game plays out as a text-message conversation. You are Majd, who has stayed behind in Syria while his wife Nour, a migrant, travels toward Europe. As the two chat on a messaging app much like WhatsApp, you advise her as best you can, and the path she takes depends partly on what you suggest. The story follows her perilous journey as she tries to reach safety.

The title is a Syrian farewell that roughly means you must not die before the speaker does, and it gains weight when Majd says it to Nour. Co-produced by ARTE, Figs and The Pixel Hunt, it is single-player and serious in tone.
809240:
As a young graffiti artist, you slip past police surveillance to spray walls in some of the world's best-known cities, including Paris, Tokyo, Berlin and New York. It is a turn-based infiltration game, so each level is a puzzle about timing and positioning, and the walls get harder to reach as you go.

The setting draws on real street art. You can bomb your tag, paint childlike figures or write poems in styles inspired by artists such as Blek Le Rat, Keith Haring, Lady Pink and Miss.Tic. Cosmografik developed it, with ARTE among its producers. It is single-player and suits puzzle and stealth fans with an interest in street art.
811270:
Momentum is the main tool in this first-person platformer built around speed and nerve. You launch force fields that change how fast you and your surroundings move, using the physics to cross 25 levels that steadily get harder. Expect to rely on quick reflexes, because the game is designed to be demanding.

Beyond the story mode, which has a science-fiction plot and jokey dialogue, there is a Competitive mode ranked on Steam leaderboards and a Speedrun mode that adds a timer. Driving Force Games made it for solo play, and it suits precision platformer fans who like chasing times and ranks.
812140:
Set in Ancient Greece during the struggle between Sparta and Athens, Assassin's Creed Odyssey is an open-world action RPG in which you play a Spartan warrior. You roam islands and cities, fight on land and at sea, and rise from outcast to legendary figure while searching for the truth about your past.

Decisions carry weight here: alliances, conflicts and the fates of certain characters shift according to what you choose. You can tailor your gear, your ship and your special abilities to suit how you like to fight, and the large clashes between the two city-states can involve 150 soldiers per side. It is a single-player game that suits players who like big historical settings with room to roam.
812550:
Momentum drives this precision platformer. You run and jump across the ruins of forgotten kingdoms, then glide through the air with a physics-based flight mechanic, working toward the truth about a world a tyrant has kept hidden from its people.

The story arrives without any text, told through visuals and movement alone, and the music and sound effects shift in response to how you move. Five worlds drawn with colorful silhouettes draw on Roman, Mayan and Southeast Asian influences. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to players who enjoy flowing, artistic platforming and a quiet, wordless style of storytelling.
8140:
Ruins around the globe, from the Thailand coast to frozen Arctic islands and Mexican jungles, draw Lara Croft in search of the ancient mysteries hidden beneath them. Play centers on exploration: you climb, swing and leap through each environment, and use objects in your surroundings to open up new routes.

Every level works as a multi-stage puzzle, so progress depends as much on reading the space as on quick reflexes. Released in 2008 by Crystal Dynamics, it is a single-player adventure with full controller support. It suits players who enjoy acrobatic traversal and environmental puzzle-solving, and those curious about an earlier chapter in the long-running Tomb Raider series.
815370:
Dropped into the Amazon rainforest with almost nothing, you have to stay alive. You craft tools, hunt and forage for food, build a shelter, and look after both your body and your mind, inspecting yourself for injuries and keeping your sanity from slipping. The campaign follows anthropologist Jake Higgins as he looks for Mia, his missing wife, and runs for more than 25 hours.

The survival systems lean on real-world techniques, and the jungle is unforgiving. You can face it alone or bring friends along in online co-op, which shifts the mood from isolated dread to shared problem-solving. It suits players who like slow, demanding survival games with a story attached.
828740:
You play Rex, a veteran cop turned private detective, in this pixel-art adventure unfolding in a cyberpunk city beneath a sky-high metropolis where the neon never goes dark. You examine scenes, collect evidence and talk to the people around you while working a murder case tied to a robot uprising and to a series of killings from thirteen years earlier.

The world is dense with objects to inspect and small hidden jokes, and the tone mixes hard-boiled noir with humor, including a gang of scheming cats. It is a single-player game with a retro look, suited to players who like examining every detail of a setting and piecing a mystery together.
829280:
Styled after 1990s console classics, this 2D platformer begins when a curse sweeps across the Crystal Islands and Kaze sets out to rescue her friend Hogo, running and jumping through levels full of angry, animated vegetables.

The hook is the set of Wild Masks, each granting an animal ability: the tiger pounces, the eagle takes to the air, the lizard sprints and the shark handles water. With more than thirty main levels and over fifty bonus stages, there is plenty to work through, all drawn in hand-animated pixel art. The platforming aims to feel smooth while still posing a real challenge, so it suits fans of classic side-scrollers who want a firm test.
853050:
Spaghetti-western stealth drives this adventure about a six-year-old boy. After bandits destroy his family's farm, he is left at a remote monastery for safety, but he slips away to find his mother. You guide him through the monastery, a harsh desert, then a frontier town riddled with crime, avoiding the people who would catch him.

Because the hero is a small child, you succeed by sneaking and outwitting rather than fighting. As his confidence grows, he picks up more tricks for getting past enemies. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits players who prefer patient, tension-driven stealth with a western atmosphere and an emotional journey at its core.
870780:
This edition of CONTROL collects the main game together with the add-ons AWE and The Foundation. The core is a third-person action-adventure set inside a secretive government agency, the Bureau, which has been overrun by a hostile supernatural presence. As Jesse Faden you move through shifting, unpredictable interiors, fighting with a mix of gunplay and supernatural powers while treating the environment as a weapon.

Developer Remedy Entertainment brings its layered storytelling and strange world-building to an interconnected, open-ended layout. It is a single-player game with full controller support, aimed at players who enjoy atmospheric, mysterious settings and combat that relies on telekinetic abilities as much as on firearms.
871420:
Randomly generated levels inspired by H.P. Lovecraft's fiction make up this action roguelite, in which you play an investigator. You fight cultists and creatures from the Mythos, solve puzzles, upgrade weapons and gear, and gather the clues and knowledge needed to stand against the Great Old Ones. Settings include a creepy Victorian mansion, an abandoned hospital and a jungle where forgotten rituals take place.

Because levels are generated anew, each run plays differently, and the RPG elements let you build up your character over time. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to players who enjoy cosmic horror themes inside a roguelite loop and like combining combat with investigation.
871980:
Part visual novel and part turn-based tactical RPG, this game begins when a school trip goes astray and Takuma Momozuka and his friends are pulled into a strange world where hostile monsters roam, and they have to find a way home. Story scenes make up a large share of play, with conversations and decisions that can turn grim, and between them you explore odd locations and recruit Digimon as partners.

Your choices shape the bonds you form with other characters and feed into how the game plays. The tone is serious and sometimes harsh, built around friendship and survival, so it suits players who enjoy character-driven drama paired with tactical battles rather than fast action.
874260:
Built around a time loop, this narrative adventure sends you into ancient Rome. After finding an underground ruin, your character is carried back two thousand years to a cursed city: if a single resident sins, everyone dies. You question the townspeople, gather information and use the loop to try again with what you have learned, working out who destroyed the city and why.

The mystery is non-linear, with several possible endings and moral dilemmas that carry real consequences. Combat is available but is not the main route to solutions; conversation and deduction matter more. It is a single-player game with full controller support, well suited to players who enjoy dialogue-driven mysteries and the satisfaction of exploiting a reset.
882020:
Based on the 2018 AMA Supercross Championship, this racing sim builds its career mode around a weekly agenda: between race weekends you take on challenges, meet fans and bring in sponsors, building your rider's reputation and unlocking new content. A free-roam area called the Compound lets you practice starts, braking, cornering and scrubbing against rivals on four tracks.

More than eighty official riders from the 250SX and 450SX classes appear, with Eli Tomac making his series debut, and you can customize your own rider. Online PvP sits alongside the single-player career, and full controller support makes it a natural fit for motorsport fans who want bike racing that mixes career management with technical riding.
883710:
Capcom's RE Engine powers this reimagining of the original survival horror game, which swaps the fixed camera for a view over the shoulder and updates the controls. Leon Kennedy, a new police officer, and Claire Redfield, a student, arrive in Raccoon City just as an outbreak turns its residents into zombies. You explore dangerous buildings, solve puzzles and manage limited supplies, with each character following a storyline of their own.

Tension comes from cautious exploration and close encounters rather than constant firefights. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to horror fans who like atmospheric, deliberate pacing, as well as newcomers who want an entry point into the Raccoon City story.
8850:
Roughly ten years after the first game, this sequel returns to Rapture, the city beneath the Atlantic. You play a Big Daddy, one of the city's armored guardians, moving through its decaying halls to learn who is taking little girls from the coast and bringing them below. As a first-person shooter, it combines conventional weapons with Plasmid powers and tonics.

A separate multiplayer mode works as a prequel set during Rapture's fall, casting you as a test subject for Plasmids at Sinclair Solutions. The single-player campaign carries a moody atmosphere and a story about the city's past. It suits players who enjoyed the setting of the original, and full controller support is included for those who prefer a pad.
889260:
Bonkies is a physics-driven party game in which a crew of space monkeys builds structures across the cosmos. Each player straps on a banana-powered jetpack and a robotic arm, then grabs blocks and stacks them inside a marked outline to finish projects such as lunar habitats, rockets and hotels adrift in space. Some jobs call for less conventional tools than a simple stack.

Up to four players can share one screen in couch co-op, and a single-player mode is also available. The humor is silly, and the fun comes from coordinating with friends while everything wobbles and drifts. It suits groups looking for a lighthearted, chaotic cooperative game, with full controller support for playing on a shared couch.
889910:
Nate is a demon with famously poor taste, and in this crude 3D platformer he has been sent to collect revolting ingredients for Satan's birthday pie. Chained to him is Nugget, a pet angel who offers advice and doubles as both a grappling hook and a swinging weapon. Along the way Nate finds horns that give him new demonic abilities.

You travel through bizarre, over-the-top environments and meet outlandish characters, with humor aimed squarely at players who enjoy crude, irreverent comedy. It is a single-player game with full controller support, best for fans of 3D platformers with a collecting focus who want a deliberately tasteless tone.
890220:
Basic arithmetic practice turns into play in this small educational game. It covers addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, counting and comparison, with each category split into ten levels. A demo version limits players to three levels per category, and the listing says it was tested on Windows 7 and later.

The content is tightly focused, so it works as a simple practice tool rather than a broad game. It is single-player, and the publisher presents it as suitable for any age group. It fits parents or teachers who want an uncomplicated way for learners to rehearse number skills, and anyone who prefers short, clearly organized exercises to open-ended play.
8930:
Guiding a civilization from the earliest settlements to the space age is the goal of this turn-based strategy game. You found cities, research technology, negotiate with or fight rival leaders drawn from history, and aim to become the world's dominant power on a map of hexagonal tiles.

The interface is designed to welcome newcomers, while veterans of the series get depth and control. Multiplayer is available online and over a local network, and the game supports mods, with player-made maps, scenarios and interface changes available to add. It is single-player at heart, and it suits anyone who enjoys long, absorbing campaigns where every turn feeds a larger plan.
899310:
This tactical combat puzzler pairs the careful planning of turn-based play with the pace of real-time action. You lead a party of two characters through encounters in which skills and terrain both matter: light enemies on fire and use the farmland around them, or rig a trap that brings a tree down on your target.

The central mechanic is time control. At any moment you can rewind up to five seconds, test a different sequence of moves and keep adjusting until the fight goes your way. That makes each battle feel like a puzzle with several valid solutions. It is a single-player game for players who enjoy experimenting with tactics and retrying tricky moments.
910630:
Romance and arcade culture meet in this visual novel, which takes place in an alternate 20XX where the video game crash of 1983 never happened. After a rough run of jobs, your character starts work at the Funplex arcade, a busy place full of distinctive employees and customers.

You design your own protagonist, including pronouns, hairstyle, skin tone and eye color, and those choices carry through the art and the story. Roleplay-style decisions shape your personality and your relationships, whether they stay friendly, platonic or turn romantic. It is single-player with full controller support, and it suits readers who enjoy dialogue-heavy stories, retro arcade nostalgia and a lot of say in who their character becomes.
91200:
Tower defense is turned around in this action-strategy game: instead of building turrets, you are the one attacking them. In a near-future Earth overrun by aliens, you command an armored squad along city streets, including Baghdad and Tokyo, where huge enemy turrets guard every approach. You choose the route and decide which units to deploy, and you also control the Commander, whose abilities help the squad through tight spots.

The result is a fast, tactical blend of action and strategy. Besides the story campaign, two Squad Assault modes offer extra challenge. It is a single-player game with full controller support, suited to strategy fans who like to plan a path and adapt on the fly.
914020:
Darkham is a town with a murky past where odd cults keep appearing, and this comedy cosmic horror point-and-click game unfolds there. Don R. Ketype, a detective, is hunting the Necronomicon, but librarian Buzz Kerwan finds it first and accidentally changes Kitteh, his cat, into a creature that walks and talks. You switch between three protagonists as the story travels across the world, solving puzzles and unraveling old conspiracies.

The look is distinctive: hand-painted HD art with traditional animation, made by a studio in Transylvania. The writing leans on jokes and Lovecraft-inspired touches rather than scares. It is single-player and suits fans of classic adventure games who like a lengthy story and humor-driven puzzles.
914890:
Cats run the crime scene in this comedy-noir adventure, played in a style the developers call point-and-lick. You are Cuddles Nutterbutter, a cat private investigator working in Meow Meow Furrington, a city of cats with a serious crime problem. With your assistant, you take a last-minute case from the Chief of Police: a murder that could upset the balance between two rival crime families, the Catulets and the Montameeuws.

You explore varied locations, meet eccentric characters and solve puzzles, with plenty of cat puns along the way. It is a single-player game suited to adventure fans who enjoy light-hearted, pun-heavy humor and a noir setting played for laughs.
916350:
Four characters take turns exploring an isolated Sardinian village shadowed by an age-old ritual in this third-person horror adventure. Each has a distinct ability suited to a different kind of exploration or investigation, and together they uncover an intergenerational story rooted in local folklore.

The village is a maze, and you get little guidance. Along the way you pick up tools, work out puzzles and unlock shortcuts to new areas. When every character has died, the layout reshuffles into a new form, so the map never stays fully familiar. It is single-player with full controller support, aimed at horror fans who like disorientation, self-directed exploration and a story pieced together slowly.
916730:
Piloting an armored mech suit, a cat explores an alien underground outpost in this Metroidvania. The mission is to rescue a stranded captain whose ship has crashed. You blast and dash through enemies, face the guardians posted around the base, and search out better weapons and equipment while uncovering what happened at the facility before you arrived.

The mech can be left behind, and the cat alone can squeeze through narrow tunnels and swim through waterways, though it is far more vulnerable outside the suit. The art is pixel work with a limited palette. It is single-player with full controller support, a good match for players who like exploration-driven action with a distinctive feline twist.
919410:
Death's dancing agent takes the lead in this 3D puzzle game. As Felix, you must see that people die on schedule, working only from the shadows. Levels are grid-based platforms where each square is lit or shaded, and by rotating the sun and shifting objects you reshape where the shadows fall, create safe paths and steer each target into a fatal accident.

The developers compare its simple grid logic to Hitman Go, Monument Valley and Sokoban. The tone is darkly comic, with Felix secretly in love with Life. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to puzzle fans who like methodical thinking and morbid humor.
921800:
The story takes place in an alternate 1970s around the Dome, a vast unexplained structure found in a desert. As a CRONUS Corporation recruit, you head inside to recover artifacts, dodging radiation fields, anomalies and hostile creatures. Turn-based tactical combat, crafting and dialogue each get serious space, and your character build decides which approach works best.

Five divisions of the company, plus other factions, offer different starting paths and ways to play. It is an isometric, single-player role-playing game in the tradition of classic Fallout and Wasteland, with a grim tone and a heavy emphasis on choices and consequences. Best for fans of deep character-driven RPGs who enjoy methodical tactics and exploring a strange, hazardous setting.
926580:
A squad goes down in hostile territory in an alternate version of Eastern Europe during the Second World War, and the survivors must make their way home with little support. The war weighs on the soldiers as much as the enemy does, so how you handle the group matters as much as how you fight. Combat is turn-based, and teamwork is the main way to stay alive.

The included expansion adds a supernatural strand in which the fallen rise, giving the squad three-way fights against living enemies and the undead. From the studios BirdIsland and PortaPlay, this single-player, story-driven tactics game has a grim tone and suits players who like squad management and narrative alongside careful tactical combat.
940680:
Bullet hell meets typing in this game starring Ray Bibbia, an exorcist for hire who works through a city overrun by demons while confronting his own sinful past. To banish each enemy you type out an exorcism, using a keyboard or a gamepad, while simultaneously weaving through dense patterns of projectiles.

Boss battles drive the action, and the cast and humor lean toward the absurd, with bad jokes, a metal singer and even the Pope turning up. It is single-player with full controller support. It suits players who enjoy a demanding coordination challenge and irreverent comedy, and who like the idea of doing two difficult things at once.
941570:
Stranded in the abandoned Chandra Base on the Moon, you play a physicist whose tools are magnetism and gravity in this first-person puzzle game. By manipulating both, you solve physics-based puzzles that open the way through the base and the terraformed craters around it. The stakes are personal, since your daughter's life depends on your scientific skill.

You can push straight ahead toward safety or take time to gather clues about the politics of the 22nd-century Moon and the secret hidden in the lunar craters. It is single-player with full controller support, suited to puzzle fans who enjoy experimenting with physics rules and a sci-fi mystery that unfolds as they explore.
944430:
This post-apocalyptic mix of brawler and tower defense is built around dogs, which are mysteriously vanishing while humanity is busy with mutants and survival. You play Alpha, who discovers he can understand a rescued pup named T. Juan, and together they fight through hordes of enemies and bosses in search of answers about the vanished dogs.

Rescued dogs of different breeds join your side, each with its own traits; the Newfoundland, for example, has a healing passive. A second player can join on the same screen, and full controller support is included. The tone is playful and pun-heavy, so it suits dog lovers and couch co-op duos who want action with light strategy.
952060:
Jill Valentine tries to escape Raccoon City in this survival horror game, one of the last people left who saw what Umbrella did there. To silence her, Umbrella sends its secret weapon, Nemesis, a relentless pursuer that stalks her through the ruined streets. You move through the city in third person, fighting infected, solving light puzzles and managing ammunition.

Bundled with it is Resident Evil Resistance, an online asymmetric mode in which four survivors face a Mastermind who controls the environment and its threats. The campaign is single-player, and the online mode is player-versus-player, with full controller support throughout. It suits players who want survival horror with a strong action emphasis.
960910:
The hunt for the Origami Killer, a murderer who leaves folded paper figures at crime scenes, drives this interactive thriller. The story runs across four days and is told through four playable characters, each pursuing their own leads and motives as they try to stop the killer from claiming another victim.

Play centers on exploration, dialogue and timed button prompts rather than traditional combat, and the decisions you make shape how events unfold. Developed by Quantic Dream, it is a single-player game with full controller support and a heavy focus on story. It suits players who enjoy cinematic, character-driven drama and are comfortable with a slower, more film-like pace.
960990:
Many years of Jodie Holmes's life, from childhood onward, unfold in this cinematic thriller. Jodie is linked to Aiden, a supernatural entity, and that bond makes her both powerful and an outsider. You guide her through the dangers and losses that come with this connection as she tries to learn who she is, with action sequences, investigation and quiet character moments all playing a part.

The cast is led by Willem Dafoe and Elliot Page. The choices and actions you take influence where Jodie's story goes. Co-op allows a second player to take control of Aiden alongside the first, though the game is fully playable alone. It suits players who value cinematic, character-led storytelling over mechanical complexity.
968370:
Sent on a divine mission, the apostle Bartholomeus must free the city of Rotbork from corruption and confront the Great Evil hiding inside it in this point-and-click adventure, which you play from his perspective. The job proves harder than he expected. You explore the city across 99 hand-drawn panels, hunting for small details and solving puzzles and mini-games along the way.

The presentation follows a comic book style with animated storytelling, and the story, while serious in direction, makes room for humor. It is a single-player game for fans of classic point-and-click adventures who like a contemplative pace and detail-rich scenes.
970830:
This humorous tactical RPG draws on the Naheulbeuk universe of French writer John Lang, which began as a popular audio comedy series spoofing role-playing games and fantasy tropes. It marks the first time the story reaches English-speaking players, and also its first appearance as a game. You lead seven classic fantasy archetypes, including a Ranger, an Elf, a Dwarf, a Barbarian, a Magician and an Ogre, who barely tolerate each other while hunting a dungeon's treasure.

Their skills complement each other as they level up, so building a balanced team matters. The tone is silly and self-aware, which suits players who enjoy fantasy parody, quirky characters and tactical party combat. It is single-player with full controller support.
973580:
Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts casts you as a hired assassin who takes on contracts, each with clear objectives and a fixed payout, plus optional bonus challenges for extra money. Missions play out over large, open-ended maps where you choose how to approach each target, relying on stealth, patience and precise long-range shots. Rival snipers can interfere with your plans, so watch your surroundings.

Earnings go toward upgrades, and gadgets such as drones and remote sniper turrets widen your options, while an AR mask scans the area and highlights weak points. A dynamic reticle system aims for realistic shooting. The campaign is built for single-player, and it suits players who prefer methodical, tactical shooting to run-and-gun action.
973760:
Queen Meve of Lyria and Rivia, a war veteran, is pulled back onto the battlefield by a Nilfgaardian invasion in this single-player RPG from CD Projekt Red, which takes place in the universe of The Witcher. Between fights you travel the Northern Realms, exploring locations, making story choices and solving puzzles, and you lead her army in card battles.

The campaign runs around 30 hours and leans on narrative, with decisions that carry consequences. The tone is dark, centered on war and revenge. It suits players who enjoy Witcher lore, story-driven RPGs and card combat that doubles as tactical puzzles, and full controller support makes it comfortable on a pad.
976310:
Brutal, graphically violent bouts define this entry in the long-running fighting series from NetherRealm Studios, which pits fresh faces against returning Klassic Fighters. A movie-style story mode carries the saga through the franchise's history.

A key addition is Custom Character Variations, which give you more control over how your fighter is set up instead of locking you into one fixed version. You can play alone or compete in online player-versus-player matches, and full controller support is included. It suits fighting game fans, newcomers curious about the series, and anyone who enjoys over-the-top violence paired with a story campaign.
978300:
This remaster revisits an open-world crime game in which the Third Street Saints, once a street gang, are now a household brand. Their fame draws the attention of the Syndicate, a criminal fraternity that demands tribute, and the Saints refuse to kneel, taking the fight to Syndicate forces across the city of Steelport.

The update refreshes the visuals with better lighting, rebuilt environments and new effects. The game embraces outrageous, over-the-top humor and mature content, with a sandbox of missions and activities to roam through. You can play alone or team up in online co-op, and full controller support is included. It suits players who prefer chaotic, irreverent action to a serious crime drama.
978520:
